issues.description: At full articulation the dump-body canopy lip cuts into the cab's rear corner. This happens in normal driving: turn=±1 reaches full lock after about 2.2 s at 0.35 rad/s, and showcase.py swings the articulation joint through its full range. A real ADT body never touches the cab. The checker misses it because its overlap test only runs in the init pose.
issues.evidence: FK sweep with checks.obb_penetration, dump at 0: at articulation ±0.785 the cab shell (front_frame shape 30, collision box) and the canopy lip (dump_body shape 9, collision beam) overlap by 0.12 m. The rear ROPS pillars (shapes 39/40) overlap it by 0.145 m. At ±0.70 the overlap is still 0.052–0.074 m; it clears at ±0.60. The canopy tip sits about 0.33 m behind the hinge, while the cab's rear corner, seen from the rear frame at 45°, is about 0.52 m behind it. The 'full left articulation — top' panel and my zoomed top view both show the body corner over the cab corner. Self-collision is off in the env, so physics is unaffected, but the clash is visible in any external view.
issues.suggested_fix: Shorten the canopy lip: change `beam((BODY_FRONT - 0.05, 1.43), (BODY_FRONT + 0.32, 1.47), 2.76, 0.10)` to end at BODY_FRONT + 0.12. I checked this: the worst penetration against front_frame at ±0.785 becomes −0.049 m, i.e. about 5 cm of clearance. It also brings the raised height down from 6.92 m to about 6.75 m. Alternatives are chamfering the lip's front corners or moving PIVOT about 0.2 m rearward.

issues.description: While tipping, the body sills and tail kick-up swing down into the rear-frame rails and rear crossmember, which run 0.15–0.30 m past the body pivot. The checker never flags this because rear_frame and dump_body are parent and child, and that pair is always skipped.
issues.evidence:
Collision-shape penetration between rear_frame and dump_body, ignoring the pivot boss and lugs:
- rails (rear_frame shapes 1/2) vs sills (dump_body 2/3): 0.015 m at q=0, 0.116 at 0.6, 0.17 at 0.8, 0.23 at 1.22.
- rear crossmember (rear_frame 4) vs sills: 0.22 m at 1.22.
- rails vs tail kick-up (dump_body 7): 0.063 m at 1.22.
Cause: rails span x −0.80 to −5.85 and the crossmember sits at −5.70 (rel. hinge), while PIVOT x is −5.55. The sills start at body x = −0.40, behind the pivot, so they rotate downward as the body tips.
issues.suggested_fix:
Put the rail ends, crossmember and sill starts ahead of the pivot. I checked this layout and found zero clash (>1 cm) at q = 0, 0.4, 0.8 and 1.22:
- rails: end at PIVOT[0] + 0.10 (−5.45), i.e. box length 4.65 centred at −3.125.
- rear crossmember: move to PIVOT[0] + 0.25.
- sills: start at body x = +0.15, i.e. box 4.45 long centred at 2.375.
Keep a short pivot bracket under the boss, and move the tail lights onto it or below the kick-up line.

issues.description: The mirror heads show up in the left and right camera images as a large dark bar in the near-field corner. The builder's report says the mirror heads are out of frame, but they are not.
issues.evidence: I ray-cast at 224×224 with the env intrinsics (focal 10 mm, aperture 20.955 mm, 92.7° HFOV, near clip 0.1 m). front_frame shape 47 (left mirror head, box 0.05×0.16×0.32 at (−0.17, 1.16, 2.02)) fills 2.72% of the left image, lower-left corner, under 0.6 m away. Shape 48 does the same in the right image, lower-right. It appears in every pose (init, full tip, full lock). The camera is only 0.08 m above the mirror-head top, and the head's forward-outboard corner falls inside the pitched-down frustum.
issues.suggested_fix:
Any one of these clears it (0 mirror pixels, checked):
- raise the side cameras to z = MIRROR[2] + 0.39 (+0.15 m),
- move them outboard to y = ±(MIRROR[1] + 0.10),
- move them forward to x = MIRROR[0] + 0.10.
Raising by 0.15 m keeps the current outward-forward view.

issues.description: Height with the body raised is 6.92 m, against about 6.4–6.5 m for the real CAT 730 / A30G (+7%). This is documented in the docstring.
issues.evidence: bounding_box at dump_joint = 1.22 gives z_max 6.922 m AGL, set by the canopy-lip tip. The tail clears the ground by 0.571 m.
issues.suggested_fix: Shortening the lip (must_fix item 1) gets most of the way, to about 6.75 m. Update the docstring number afterwards.

issues.description: No onboard camera ever sees the dump body. A 'raise/lower dump body' instruction therefore shows up only in proprioceptive state, never in the images. The other haulers (rigid_haul_truck, wheel_tractor_scraper) use the same outward-forward side layout, so this is a dataset-wide choice.
issues.evidence: In the ray-cast front/left/right images at init, full tip and full lock, dump_body covers 0% of every image. The front camera looks over the hood; the side cameras are at yaw ±0.60, pitch 0.30.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional. Yaw the side cameras rearward like real mirrors (about ±2.6 rad, small pitch) so the body tip and the articulated rear frame are visible, or record the decision in notes.

issues.description: The empty mass split is about 49/51 front/rear axle. Real ADTs carry roughly 55% or more on the front axle when empty (engine, transmission and cab are all on the tractor). This has no effect in the kinematic, gravity-off env.
issues.evidence: Link COMs give a combined COM at x = −3.04 m, i.e. front axle 11.5 t of 23.46 t (49.2%). front_frame is 10.2 t and the rear frame plus body is 9.0 t.
issues.suggested_fix: Optionally shift about 1 t from rear_frame/dump_body to front_frame (e.g. front 11.2 t, rear frame 3.7 t, body 4.3 t).

issues.description: Style differs from hydraulic_excavator.py. build() runs a coordinate-descent optimiser (_hoist_fit) on every call and checks a geometric invariant with a bare assert, which disappears under python -O. There are four helpers instead of a single build(). The docstring gives height 3.43 m while the envelope says 3.44 m.
issues.evidence: Lines 82–133 hold the _hoist_fit optimiser and line 257 the `assert BARREL_LEN - ... > 0.15`. build() still takes only 9 ms, so this is about readability, not speed.
issues.suggested_fix: Either freeze the fitted k, c, ks, cs as module constants, with a comment saying how they were derived (and keep _hoist_fit as a check), or keep the fit and replace the assert with `if ...: raise ValueError(...)`. Make the docstring height and the envelope agree.

core_issues: checks.py self-overlap test: (a) it only evaluates the init pose, so clashes at tool limits or full articulation/steer go unreported (the ADT canopy into the cab at ±0.785 is 0.12–0.145 m); (b) it skips every parent/child pair outright, so the ADT body sills diving 0.23 m into the rear-frame rails at full tip are never seen. Suggested fix: also evaluate the pose at each tool's lower/upper limit and at ±full articulation/steer, and for adjacent pairs skip only shapes within about 0.3 m of the joint origin, or add per-shape allowances.

checks.py has no camera near-field occlusion check. Builders verify this by hand and can get it wrong, as with the ADT mirror heads at 2.7% of the side images. Add a cheap ray-cast or projection check that fails if more than about 1% of a camera's pixels hit machine geometry within about 0.5 m.

I confirm the builder's glass finding. DEFAULT_MATERIALS['glass'] has alpha 1.0 and urdf_builder writes it unchanged, so panes are opaque. On hydraulic_excavator the front camera is 0.09 m behind its windscreen with pitch 0.35. Rays more than about 0.3 rad below the optical axis reach the pane at a depth of ≥0.108 m, past the 0.1 m near clip, so the lower part of the HEX front image shows a solid blue pane. Either make glass translucent and confirm the URDF importer honours alpha, or require cab cameras to sit outside the glass.
I confirm the urdf_builder.build_urdf header comment names 'scripts/heavy_machines/generate.py', which does not exist; check_machine.py and write_assets generate the files.

I agree with the builder: followers are linear only (q = k*q_src + c), so a two-pin hydraulic cylinder over a large stroke cannot stay pinned at both ends. A follower kind that aims a link at a point on another link, or polynomial follower coefficients, would remove the per-machine workarounds.

result.summary:
Telehandler (telehandler, TH, lifting), modelled on a JCB 540-170 Loadall (CAT TH514D class). `check_machine.py telehandler` prints OK (0 errors, 1 warning) and wrote the URDF and JSON assets. test_machines.py passes (18 tests) and test_env_logic.py passes (9 tests), including every telehandler subtest.

Files: /home/user/vla-datagen/scripts/heavy_machines/machines/telehandler.py (only file edited) and /home/user/vla-datagen/assets/heavy_machines/telehandler/{telehandler.urdf, telehandler.json}.

Dimensions and mass:
- Travel-pose bounding box 7.63 × 2.48 × 2.69 m vs envelope 7.56 × 2.44 × 2.69 m (+0.9 %, +1.6 %, 0 %).
- Mass 12,060 kg, exactly the operating mass: chassis 7,180 (frame, axles, cab, engine bay, counterweight, stabilisers); 4 wheels × 280; 2 front knuckles × 60; boom base 1,300 / mid 1 700 / mid 2 520 / fly 430; carriage 420 + levelling frame 20; lift ram barrel 160 + rod 90.
- Root height 0.655 m (rear-axle centre); wheels touch the ground; forks 0.12–0.14 m above the ground; everything else at least 0.40 m up.

Layout:
- Cab on the left (+y) with glass panes: windscreen, door, lower front, both sides, rear and roof.
- Boom pivot at the rear, low (x = -1.30 m, 1.75 m above ground, y = -0.12), boom running down the right side of the cab.
- Engine bay with louvred grille and exhaust on the right; cooling pack behind the right rear wheel, hydraulic tank behind the left one.
- Rear counterweight with lights, bumper, tow pin and number plate; folded front stabilisers.
- Front mudguards with road lights that steer with the wheels.
- Four 500/70 R24 tyres (wheel_link) on a 2.75 m wheelbase, 1.94 m track.

Drive: Ackermann, front-wheel steer, fixed_axle_x = 0 (rear axle), wheelbase 2.75 m, max_speed 8.5 m/s (same in reverse), max_steer 0.65 rad, steer_rate 0.25 rad/s. Steer joints are limited to ±0.85 rad; the inner wheel reaches 46.1° at max_steer. turn = +1 turns left (the env test confirms the yaw increases).

Tools (all role "tool"):
- boom_luff (boom_luff_joint, revolute, axis (0,-1,0)): -0.127 to +1.209 rad (69.3°), init -0.127, 0.14 rad/s; raise/lower, auto-verified.
- boom_telescope (boom_telescope_joint, prismatic): 0 to 3.712 m PER SECTION, 0.30 m/s; extend/retract, auto-verified. boom_mid_2_joint and boom_fly_joint follow it with k = 1, so total extension is 11.14 m.
- fork_tilt (fork_tilt_joint, revolute): -1.25 to +0.40 rad, init 0.05, 0.45 rad/s; +1 = tilt_back (fork tips up), -1 = tilt_forward. The angle is relative to level because carriage_level_joint follows boom_luff with k = -1 (carriage compensation); FK confirms the forks stay exactly level at every luff angle when fork_tilt = 0.

Other followers: lift_cylinder_joint and lift_rod_joint (the visible lift ram, linear fit to the luff joint).

Geometry checked by forward kinematics: fork underside 16.70 m at full luff and full extension (datasheet 16.7 m); reach 12.50 m from the front tyres to the fork heel at boom 0° and full extension (datasheet 12.5 m).

Cameras, all on the chassis:
- front: operator eye point 2.05 m above the ground, just ahead of the windscreen (glass panes are opaque boxes in Isaac, so it sits outside them); pitch 0.18, yaw -0.15. Sees the boom and the carriage in the travel pose and at mid-height lifts.
- left: cab front-left roof corner, pitch 0.35, yaw +0.65.
- right: post on the front-right corner of the engine cover, 1.88 m up, pitch 0.32, yaw -0.75.

Visual checks: zoomed orthographic, 3D and approximate camera-image renders of the travel, mid-lift and full-luff poses, plus the standard poses and sweeps PNGs.
result.datasheet:
JCB 540-170 figures, from web-search summaries of the JCB spec sheet and hire/dealer listings. The JCB PDF itself could not be downloaded (the proxy returned 403 and DNS failed). Sources: [cdn2.antbuildz.com 540-170 spec sheet](https://cdn2.antbuildz.com/images/540-170.pdf), [Ardent Hire 17 m telehandlers](https://www.ardenthire.com/plant-hire/telehandlers/17-metre), [JCB 540-170 product page](https://www.jcb.com/en-AE/products/machines/telescopic-handlers/540-170/), [APS Equipment listing](https://www.apsequipment.co.nz/product/17m-jcb-540-170-telehandler/).

Datasheet values used:
- Max lift height 16.7 m; max forward reach 12.5 m; max payload 4.0 t.
- Operating mass 12,060 kg (listings range 11.2–12.3 t; I used the spec-sheet figure rather than the ~11 t in the brief).
- Overall length 6.36 m to the carriage face and 5.08 m to the front tyres. The envelope uses 7.56 m because the 1.2 m pallet forks are included.
- Overall width 2.44 m over tyres; overall height 2.69 m; wheelbase 2.75 m.
- Stabiliser width deployed 3.55 m (stabilisers modelled folded, not driven); 4-speed powershift.

Assumed / typical for the class:
- Top speed ≈ 30 km/h, giving max_speed 8.5 m/s as specified.
- 500/70 R24 tyres (Ø 1.31 m, 0.50 m section), so track 1.94 m; ground clearance about 0.40 m.
- JCB side-engine layout: cab on the left, boom pivot at the rear (1.30 m behind the rear axle, 1.75 m above the ground), boom alongside the right of the cab, engine on the right.
- Four-section boom: 5.63 m retracted, 16.77 m extended pivot-to-carriage-pin (3 × 3.71 m stroke), carriage pin on a 0.30 m drop nose. I could not confirm the section count; it is consistent with the retracted and extended lengths.
- Boom luff range -7.2° to +69.3°.
- Single lift ram, 2.43 → 3.47 m pin to pin, base behind the rear axle.
- Automatic carriage compensation, so fork tilt is measured relative to level.
- Fork tilt 23° back / 72° forward.
- Cycle times: boom up ≈ 9.5 s (class 9–10 s); telescope out ≈ 12.4 s (class ≈ 13–16 s); fork tilt across its full range ≈ 3.7 s.
- Front-wheel steer only (the real machine also has 4WS and crab modes); max_steer 0.65 rad; steer rate 0.25 rad/s (2.6 s centre to lock); inner wheel 46.1°, outer 30.9°; 2WS turning radius about 5.6 m over the outer tyre.

Judgement calls:
- The telescope action moves ONE section (0 to 3.712 m) and the other two follow 1:1, so total extension is 3 × the tool position. Followers cannot chain, so total extension cannot be the action unit.
- The forks can go well below the ground in some reachable poses: luff at its minimum with full extension puts them about 1.6 m under grade, and tilting forward in the travel pose also drives them into the ground.
remaining_warnings: tool fork_tilt: directions 'tilt_back'/'tilt_forward' not auto-verifiable. Justified: neither word is in the auto-verified vocabulary, and these are the brief's suggested words (the bulldozer already uses the same style, tilt_left/tilt_right). I checked the sign visually in telehandler_sweeps.png: at the upper limit (+0.40) the fork tips rise (tilt back) and at the lower limit (-1.25) they point down (tilt forward). The joint uses axis (0,-1,0), so +q raises the forward-pointing forks.
core_issues: test/test_env_logic.py test_turn_left_increases_yaw checks the wrapped yaw (atan2 range [-pi, pi]) after 3 s at drive 0.7, turn +1. A fast-turning Ackermann machine passes pi and reads as a right turn. The telehandler with steer_rate 0.40 turned left by 3.50 rad but the test saw -2.78 and failed. Workaround: steer_rate 0.25 rad/s (left turn 2.64 rad, 0.5 rad margin). The backhoe_loader appears to have hit the same wall (it now has steer_rate 0.16). Fix: accumulate an unwrapped yaw in the test, or shorten the run.

render.py _draw_ortho paints the top and front panels in reversed order. For 'top', sgn = -1 sorts the highest shapes first, so the lowest parts (chassis belly, axles) are painted over the boom and cab, which makes it a bottom view. For 'front', the rear-most shapes (counterweight, tail lights) are painted over the front ones. The side panel is consistent: a left-side view with the front pointing right. Fix: depth sign +1 for top (paint low z first) and +1 for front (paint low x first). I used a scratch renderer with the corrected order for my visual checks.

machine_env.py Ackermann drive has no lateral-acceleration or speed-dependent steer limit. At 8.5 m/s and full lock the yaw rate is about 2.3 rad/s (about 2 g lateral), which would tip a real telehandler. An optional Drive.max_lateral_accel, scaling the steer limit with speed, would make high-speed turns realistic.

Followers are linear in their source joint (k*q + c). Visible hydraulic rams over a 76° luff range therefore miss their pins by up to about 9 cm (worst-case minimax). A nonlinear follower type (lookup table or 'aim at a point on another link') would allow exact rams.

Follower chaining is forbidden and the telescope tool joint must be the first nested section. For multi-section booms the action unit is therefore the per-section stroke (here 1/3 of the total extension) rather than total extension, which is less intuitive in the language instructions and teleop.

issues.description: No camera ever sees the backhoe or the stabilisers, so 5 of the 7 tool channels give no visual feedback: backhoe_swing, backhoe_boom, backhoe_stick, backhoe_bucket and stabilizers. All three cameras sit at the cab front and look forward (front) or forward-outward (left/right, yaw ±0.55). For a VLA data-gen machine, an instruction like 'lower the backhoe boom to 50%' then produces image sequences in which nothing visibly changes.
issues.evidence: I projected every link's visual shape points into each camera frustum (half-FOV 46.3° from focal 10 mm and aperture 20.955 mm, square image) in four poses: init; a digging pose (boom -0.3, stick 0, bucket 0.5, stabilisers down 0.45); swing +1.5 with boom 0.3 and stick 0; and the loader at full lift. In every pose, front, left and right see only chassis, loader_arm, shovel_level, loader_bucket, the lift rams and the front knuckles and wheels. swing_frame, boom, stick, backhoe_bucket, the boom and dipper rams, and both stabiliser legs score 0.00 in all three cameras.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep 'front' on the loader. Move left/right to the rear cab corners looking rear-outward and down. Tested: Camera('left', 'chassis', (CAB_X0 - 0.10, CAB_HW + 0.12, agl(2.80)), (0.0, 0.75, math.pi - 0.35)) and the mirrored right camera (y negated, yaw -(math.pi - 0.35)). In the init, dig, deep-dig and ±1.5 slew poses each one sees the swing frame (0.6-0.9), boom/stick/bucket (≈1.0 when digging or slewed to its side) and its own stabiliser leg (0.92). Neither camera sits inside any shape. This also gets rid of the current side cameras' mirror heads, which sit 0.18 m from the lens and cover the lower outer corner of each side image (u 0.22..1.0, v -1..-0.72).

issues.description: The roading (init) pose is not the real travel position, and the bucket cannot be curled from it without passing through the king post. The backhoe bucket is left almost uncurled (0.2 of its -1.10..2.45 range) and dangles 0.37 m above the ground; it is the lowest rear part, with a departure angle of about 10°. Real BHL travel position is boom up, dipper fully in, bucket fully closed. In this geometry the bucket pin sits only 0.32 m behind the swing casting, so any curl from the roading pose drives the 0.8 m bucket through the king-post casting and the boom. The sweep render shows the blue (q=2.45) bucket overlapping the boom foot. The checker misses this because it only tests the init pose, and self-collision is disabled in Isaac, so it clips silently.
issues.evidence: Collision OBB penetration of backhoe_bucket vs the non-adjacent swing_frame and boom, other joints at init: q=0.6 → swing_frame 0.07 m; q=1.0 → 0.19 m; q=1.6 → 0.22 m plus boom 0.04 m; q=2.0 → 0.29 m and 0.23 m; q=2.45 → boom 0.24 m. Bucket lowest point at q=0.2 is 0.37 m above ground (AGL). Overall length 6.05 m is set by the dipper back at x=-2.10 and the shovel lip at x=3.94.
issues.suggested_fix: Fold the dipper slightly less and roll the bucket in for transport. Tested: BOOM_INIT=1.48, STICK_LO=STICK_INIT=-1.25 and HOE_INIT=2.45 give zero bucket penetration, bucket low point 1.10 m above ground and H 3.65 m. The cost is L=6.24 m (+11 %, a warning), which could be recovered by carrying the shovel closer to the nose. Alternatively, shrink or move the swing casting collision box so a curled bucket clears it. Then re-render the backhoe_bucket sweep.

issues.description: steer_rate=0.16 rad/s (7.5 s lock to lock) was chosen to get past a flawed shared test (wrapped-yaw comparison), not from the machine class. It does not fix the physical problem it cites. Once full lock is reached the kinematic drive still yaws at 3.5 rad/s at top speed (about 4 g lateral). Meanwhile every low-speed site manoeuvre now takes 3.75 s to reach lock. Real hydrostatic BHL steering is roughly 0.25-0.4 rad/s on this virtual angle.
issues.evidence: Drive(max_speed=11.1, wheelbase=2.17, max_steer=0.60, steer_rate=0.16). At full lock: w = 11.1*tan(0.6)/2.17 = 3.50 rad/s, v*w = 38.8 m/s². The module docstring itself says 0.3 rad/s was rejected only because test_turn_left_increases_yaw wraps past π after 3 s at 70 % speed (analytically 4.74 rad at 0.3 rad/s vs 2.68 rad at 0.16). concrete_mixer_truck.py uses the same workaround (0.17).
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the shared test (compare unwrapped yaw) and/or add a lateral-acceleration cap in machine_env (see core_issues). Then restore steer_rate to about 0.3 rad/s and drop the docstring paragraph that justifies 0.16.

issues.description: The loader-arm pivot is inside the cab. A_PIN x=1.00 is 5 cm behind the cab front wall (CAB_X1=1.05), so the arm root beam and pivot boss pierce the windscreen glass at its lower corners at every lift angle. Real 3CX arm towers stand in front of the cab.
issues.evidence: Visual OBB overlap between the windscreen glass (centre x=1.05, y ±0.75) and loader_arm shapes [0]/[14] (root beam) and [4]/[18] (pivot boss, y=±0.64): 0.15/0.12 m at lift 0.11, 0.18/0.15 m at lift 0.7, 0.18/0.14 m at lift 1.42. The side render shows the arm starting inside the cab outline.
issues.suggested_fix: Move A_PIN forward to x≈1.22 (the boss radius is 0.16) and shift the towers and LC geometry with it, or move CAB_X1 back to about 0.85 and adjust the front camera x. Then recheck B_MAX_H and the 3.40 m pin height.

issues.description: The lift-ram geometry passes through dead centre. The base is at the nose and the eye is on a drop lug 0.70 m below the arm pivot, so the pin-to-pin distance first shrinks and then grows over the lift range. No hydraulic ram can drive a joint through that, and real BHL lift rams extend steadily to lift. The boom ram also peaks right at the roading pose.
issues.evidence: Lift ram pin distance at q=-0.04 / 0.11 / 0.70 / 1.42: 1.304 / 1.207 / 1.015 / 1.318 m. Boom ram at q=0 / 1.40 / 1.48: 1.108 / 1.195 / 1.186 m. The dipper ram is monotonic (1.815 → 1.245), which is fine.
issues.suggested_fix: Anchor LC_BASE low near the front axle (e.g. x≈2.2, 0.55 m above ground) and put LC_EYE on the arm's mid-section, e.g. arm frame (1.0, -0.35), so the length grows steadily by about 0.6 m over the lift range. Move BC_EYE slightly so the boom ram is still extending at BOOM_HI. Assert in build() that each ram's length is monotonic.

issues.description: The docstring and report do not match the code for the loader arm. _lift_hi() gives an upper limit of 1.423 rad, not 1.38 (docstring) or 1.383 (report). Full-range raise therefore takes 4.9 s, not the quoted 4.7 s.
issues.evidence: FK joint dump: loader_arm_joint [-0.040, 1.423], v=0.3. Raise time (1.423 + 0.04)/0.30 = 4.88 s.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the docstring to 1.42 rad. Either set the lift velocity to 0.31 rad/s for a 4.7 s raise, or quote 4.9 s.

issues.description: The direction words for backhoe_stick (out/in) and backhoe_swing (left/right) on a revolute joint produce ungrammatical language labels from tasks.py.
issues.evidence: Sampled instructions for this machine include 'out the backhoe stick to 90%', 'in the backhoe stick to 40%', 'left the backhoe swing to 90%' and 'right the backhoe swing to 0%'.
issues.suggested_fix: For the stick, use positive='extend' and negative='retract'. Both are in checks.py's auto-verified vocabulary and read correctly ('extend the backhoe stick to 90%'). The swing wording needs the shared tasks.py fix (core_issues).

issues.description: At full steering lock the front axle tube pokes into the inner tyre. The cylinder is 1.40 m long (ends at y=±0.70), only 0.22 m inboard of the zero-offset kingpin at y=±0.92. The arm knee also grazes the tyre when the shovel is on the ground.
issues.evidence: Exact point-in-cylinder sampling at the env's real inner-wheel angle of 0.767 rad (max_steer 0.6): the chassis axle tube point (2.08, 0.70, 0.51 m above ground) lies 0.067 m inside the left tyre. At lift 0 with steer 0.3, the loader_arm visual knee is 0.035 m inside it. The OBB check reports 0.16-0.24 m, but that is an over-estimate from the tyre's box bound.
issues.suggested_fix: Shorten the front axle cylinder to about 1.20 m (ends at y=±0.60) and the matching knuckle stub. Optionally raise ARM_KNEE z by about 0.05 m so the arm clears the tyre top (0.96 m above ground) at lift 0.

core_issues: machine_env.py and test_env_logic.py: test_turn_left_increases_yaw asserts on wrapped yaw (atan2), so a correct but fast turn (more than π in 3 s) fails. Separately, the Ackermann model has no yaw-rate or lateral-acceleration limit: the backhoe loader yaws at 3.5 rad/s at 11.1 m/s and full lock (about 4 g). Machine files are lowering steer_rate to get past the test (backhoe_loader 0.16, concrete_mixer_truck 0.17). Fix: accumulate unwrapped yaw in the test (or run it for 1 s), and in _apply_action clamp the steer angle so |v*w| <= about 3-4 m/s² (|tan(steer)| <= a_max*wheelbase/v²).

checks.py has no camera-coverage rule. backhoe_loader passes with no camera seeing 5 of its 7 tools. Suggest: for each Tool, project its child subtree's visual points into the three camera frustums (focal 10 mm, aperture 20.955 mm) at init and at each tool's range ends; warn (or error) if no camera sees at least ~20 % of the subtree in any of those poses.

checks.py checks self-overlap only in the init pose with steering at 0. Tool sweeps and full steering lock are never checked, so the backhoe_loader hoe bucket passing 0.19-0.29 m through the king-post casting when curled from the roading pose goes undetected. Suggest a warning-level overlap pass at each tool's lower/upper limit (others at init) and at ±max_steer per-wheel angles. Ignore pairs with a cylinder or sphere, or test cylinders exactly; the OBB bound over-reports tyre corners by about 0.15 m.

core_issues: test_env_logic.py test_turn_left_increases_yaw can fail falsely for fast short-wheelbase Ackermann machines. It checks the wrapped yaw (-π, π] after 3 s at 70 % speed with turn=+1. With a 2.17 m wheelbase, 11.1 m/s and max_steer 0.6, the machine turns about 4.75 rad left, which wraps to -1.53 rad and fails. Root cause: the drive in machine_env.py has no lateral-acceleration or yaw-rate limit (full lock at top speed gives about 3.5 rad/s, roughly 4 g). Workaround in my file only: steer_rate 0.16 rad/s, which keeps 3 s of turning under π (≈ 2.7 rad). Suggested fix: compare unwrapped yaw in the test, or cap |v·ω| in the drive model.

The URDF tree has only linear followers (q = k*q_src + c), so ram barrels and rods cannot track their pins exactly over large joint ranges. Each machine file re-implements its own cylinder fitting; this one misses by up to 12 cm at the dipper's range end. The shovel's parallel-lift tipping linkage cannot be represented, so the shovel rams are fixed on the arms. A shared 'look-at' / two-point follower role in machine_env, or a shared cylinder-fit helper in spec.py, would make rams exact and cheaper to build.

issues.evidence: The docstring says 'Bobcat T66 ≈ 4 100 kg' and 'rated operating capacity ≈ 1.2 t (35 % of tipping load)'.
issues.suggested_fix: Cite only the CAT 259D3 for the 4.08 t operating mass, or give the T66 figure as about 3.7 t. Change ROC to about 1.0–1.1 t.

issues.description: The bucket tilt cylinders, a prominent feature on real CTLs, are missing. The builder documents why: a linear follower cannot track them over 135° of tilt.
issues.evidence: The docstring and the builder's report both say the tilt cylinders were left out because of follower linearity (0.14 m best-fit error).
issues.suggested_fix: Leave it until a two-pin cylinder role exists (see core issue). Meanwhile, a short visual-only barrel stub fixed to each arm upright would bring back the silhouette without needing a connected rod.

core_issues: checks.py does not check overlaps between parent/child link pairs (the `adjacent` set) and checks only the init pose. That let a 6.8 cm (init) to 17.6 cm (full curl) arm-through-bucket penetration and a 4.7 cm cross-tube/brace overlap on the CTL pass with 0 errors. Suggested change: also test adjacent pairs, but skip shapes whose OBB contains or touches the joint origin/axis (pin bosses, ears, clevises). Sample every tool at lower/init/upper, plus a few combined poses, not only init.

Confirmed the builder's render.py claim: `_draw_ortho` has every depth sign inverted. With proj side=(0,2,1,+1), top=(0,1,2,-1), front=(1,2,0,-1), far shapes are drawn last. On the CTL's init 'front' view the rear tail lights and grille show and the bucket is hidden; the 'top' view hides the cab roof under the tracks and deck. Re-rendering with side -1, top +1, front +1 gives correct occlusion (bucket in front, roof on top). Preview-only, but reviewers and builders judge machines from these images.

Confirmed geometrically that hydraulic_excavator's front camera sits inside its solid cab box. Camera (1.15, 0.77, 1.45) in upper_structure; cab box spans x -0.45..1.25, y 0.27..1.27, z 0.35..1.74. An opaque 'glass' windscreen box sits at x 1.24..1.28, about 9–13 cm in front of the lens. In Isaac the reference machine's operator view is likely just the windscreen. Move the camera just outside the windscreen (x ≈ 1.31), as the CTL does.

Agree with the builder: followers are linear only (q = k*q_src + c), so wide-range linkage cylinders (loader and dozer tilt cylinders, excavator bucket cylinders) cannot be shown connected. A visual-only 'cylinder' role is the clean fix: the env poses barrel and rod each step from two pin points known by FK. A piecewise-linear lookup table on followers would also work.

checks.py has no auto-verification for 'curl'/'dump', so every bucket tool warns. Possible test: 'curl' = the child's +x tip (or its farthest point from the joint axis) rises when q goes from lower to upper, i.e. the existing 'raise' test applied to a tip point instead of the subtree centroid.

issues.description: The substitute parallel tilt linkage visibly clips through the lift-arm cross tube in the normal dump / truck-loading poses, right in the centre of the front (operator) camera. The tilt lever turns with the bucket over q_rel = q_bucket - 0.8*q_lift from -2.15 to +0.85 rad (172 deg relative to the arms). It pivots on P_PIN, only 0.09 m above the top face of the cross tube, so its 0.70 m L-arm, its 0.30 m U-arm and the tilt-rod eye sweep through the tube. The lever beams also have collision=True, which contradicts the notes ('tilt lever, links and cylinders are visual-only').
issues.evidence:
Measured with checks.obb_penetration on FK poses. The cross tube is the lift_arm Box 0.32x1.28x0.30 at arm-frame (1.80, -1.13).
- lift 0.6 / bucket -1.13: tilt_lever plates 0.18-0.25 m into the tube, tilt-rod eye 0.22 m.
- Max lift / full dump: plates 0.18-0.21 m, rod eye 0.12 m.
- Datasheet 45-deg dump-clearance pose (lift 1.273, bucket -1.04): plates 0.20-0.21 m, rod eye 0.15 m. The rod eye sits at arm-frame (1.64-1.79, -1.14..-1.19), inside the tube volume (x 1.64-1.96, z -1.28..-0.98).
- Ground full-curl dig pose (lift -0.03, bucket 0.82): tilt_lever enters front_frame by 0.08 m.
From the front camera at (-0.38, 0, 2.95 m AGL) the tube is about 28 deg above the optical axis at max lift, so the clipping is in frame. checks.py misses all of this because it only tests the init pose.
issues.suggested_fix:
Re-lay the lever so its sweep clears the tube.
- Raise P_PIN to at least 0.35 m above the tube top, and/or move the rod eye to the top of the lever like a real bell crank. With U_PIN at angle phi, q_rel+phi must stay outside about [-2.47, -0.67] rad, e.g. phi ~ 1.5 rad.
- Alternatively shorten the L-arm, or move CROSS_TUBE back/down toward ARM_KNEE, outside the lever circle.
- Re-run tilt_cylinder_fit() afterwards.
- Sweep obb_penetration over a 9x9 lift x bucket grid for lift_arm/front_frame vs tilt_lever/tilt_rod/tilt_cylinder, and keep it under about 3 cm in reachable non-buried poses.
- Set collision=False on the lever beams to match the notes.

issues.description: The bucket can be driven far below grade. The tool limits are independent and the env writes joints kinematically, so dumping at carry or ground height buries the cutting edge up to 1.2 m. The repo's own random task generator hits this region most of the time when a bucket goal comes first. The builder's report and docstring don't mention it.
issues.evidence:
FK, lowest bucket point above ground:
- Ground + full dump (lift -0.03, bucket -1.13): -1.23 m.
- At the init lift (0.035): bucket 0% -1.06 m, 10% -0.97, 20% -0.83, 30% -0.63, 40% -0.40, 50% -0.13, 60% +0.11.
- A full dump only clears the ground for lift >= 0.40 rad (33% of the lift range).
- tasks.sample_goals: from init the bucket is at 99%, so the only allowed first bucket goals are 0-60%. Six of those seven (0-50%) bury the bucket 0.13-1.06 m.
This can't be fixed with the current linear limits: holding the dump limit near 0 deg at the ground and -50 deg at max lift needs a ground-angle slope of about -0.62/rad of lift. Holding rack-back at 47 deg (ground) and 62 deg (max lift) needs +0.2/rad. One linear LEVEL cannot satisfy both.
issues.suggested_fix: Mainly a shared fix (see core_issues): add a ground clamp or coupled tool limits in machine_env, and FK-based goal rejection in tasks.sample_goals. In this file, state the safe region in the docstring and notes (full dump needs lift >= 0.40 rad; bucket below ~55% at carry height buries the edge). Keep LEVEL/limits as they are, since they reproduce the datasheet rack-back and dump angles.

issues.description: The drive parameters were detuned to pass a flawed shared test, and the docstring gives a false justification for it. The brief asks for max_speed ~10 m/s and articulation_rate ~0.5 rad/s, and the datasheet top speed is 37.5 km/h (10.4 m/s). The file uses 8.6 m/s and 0.35 rad/s. The docstring says the caps 'keep turns plausible', but full lock at 8.6 m/s is still physically impossible. The workaround is also fragile.
issues.evidence:
- Full lock (0.70 rad) at 8.6 m/s: yaw rate 1.87 rad/s, front-axle radius 4.59 m, lateral acceleration 1.64 g. Hardly better than 2.40 g at 10.4 m/s.
- Replaying test_turn_left_increases_yaw (3 s, 70% speed, full lock): 8.6 m/s with 0.35 rad/s gives 2.97 rad, only 0.17 rad below the pi wrap. 8.6 with 0.5 gives 3.37, wrapping to -2.91 (fails). 10.4 with 0.5 gives 4.00, wrapping to -2.29 (fails).
issues.suggested_fix: Fix the shared test (unwrapped yaw or yaw-rate sign; see core_issues), then restore max_speed 10.4 m/s and articulation_rate 0.5 rad/s, or a sourced lock-to-lock time. Until then, rewrite the docstring to say plainly that the caps are a workaround for the shared test's yaw wrap. Drop the 'plausible turns' claim, or add a real speed-dependent articulation limit in the core.

issues.description: The model height exceeds the stated envelope because of the beacon. Height is 3.52 m against an envelope of 3.42 m (+2.9%).
issues.evidence: bbox_LWH 8.35 x 2.96 x 3.52 m. The beacon cylinder sits at z1+0.05 on the ROPS roof (agl 3.42-3.52).
issues.suggested_fix: Either set envelope H to 3.52 with a note ('incl. beacon'), or lower the roof so the beacon top lands at 3.42 m. The datasheet height usually excludes the beacon, so the first is more honest.

issues.description: The left access ladder pierces the rear fender's front lip, and the ladder landing overlaps the lip. These are same-link visual shapes, so the checker can't see them.
issues.evidence: The ladder rail box at x=-0.80, y=1.07 spans z 0.42-1.78 m AGL. The fender front beam (-0.85, 1.77)->(-0.66, 1.42), 0.05 thick, spans y 0.79-1.43 and crosses x=-0.80 at z ~1.68 m. The landing box (x -0.845..-0.395, z 1.76-1.80) touches the beam's top end.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the ladder about 0.1 m forward (x -0.70/-0.36), or end the fender's front lip at x -0.75, so the rails pass in front of it.

issues.description: The code is much heavier than the reference style (one build() plus constants). The file is 641 lines and runs a coarse-to-fine minimax pattern search at every build. It also defines 20+ module helpers, several of which re-implement patterns already copied in other machine files (_follower, _cylinder_fit). _side_plate assigns a lambda to a name (PEP 8 E731).
issues.evidence: hydraulic_excavator.py is 133 lines. _follower is also defined in backhoe_loader, telehandler, bulldozer, rough_terrain_crane, mini_excavator and wheeled_excavator. _cylinder_fit is also in asphalt_paver, bulldozer, compact_track_loader, soil_compactor and wheeled_excavator. Line 298: x_edge = lambda z: ...
issues.suggested_fix: Freeze the fitted coefficients as named constants: tilt (a, b, c) = (0.821, 0.101, -0.405) and lift (k, c) = (0.568, 0.238), with lengths 2.185/2.624 and 1.459/2.511 m. Add a comment on how they were derived, or keep the fitter in a dev-only helper. Replace the lambda with a def, and move generic follower/cylinder helpers to a shared module once the core has one.

core_issues: test/test_env_logic.py test_turn_left_increases_yaw asserts on the WRAPPED yaw (env._yaw is atan2-wrapped) after 3 s at 70% speed and full lock. Any machine that yaws more than pi in 3 s fails while turning correctly. Replay for the wheel loader: 10.4 m/s with 0.5 rad/s gives 4.00 rad unwrapped, which wraps to -2.29 and fails. That forced this builder to detune top speed and articulation rate, and the shipped values pass with only 0.17 rad of margin. Fix: integrate an unwrapped yaw in the test (sum env._yaw_rate*dt), assert on the sign of env._yaw_rate, or check after 1 s.

render.py _draw_ortho uses the wrong depth sign for the 'top' and 'front' views: proj top=(0,1,2,-1.0), front=(1,2,0,-1.0). A toy spec proves it. In 'top', the box at z=2 is drawn FIRST and covered by the z=0 box, so the view is from below; the WL top panel shows axle differentials over the frame. In 'front', the x=+2 box is drawn first and the x=-2 box on top, so it shows the rear (counterweight, tail lights). Fix: use +1.0 for top and front (draw low z / low x first). The builder only reported the 'front' case.

machine_env.py has no ground or coupled tool limits: tool joints are clamped independently and written kinematically. tasks.sample_goals samples tool targets uniformly, independent of the other tools. For a loader this means routine 'dump the bucket to X%' goals at carry height bury the bucket 0.1-1.1 m underground in recorded data, and physically correct joint limits can't prevent it. Fix options: (a) in _apply_action, stop a tool's motion when FK puts any non-ground-contact collision shape below z=0 (FK is already done per step on the CPU for cameras); (b) add an optional per-machine coupled-limit hook (e.g. MachineSpec.tool_limits(q) -> (lo, hi)); (c) make sample_goals reject goals whose FK pose penetrates the ground.

checks.py validates ground clearance and self-overlap only in the init pose, and treats only direct parent/child pairs as adjacent. This machine passes cleanly while burying the bucket 1.23 m at a joint-limit corner and clipping the lever 0.25 m through the arm cross tube in normal dump poses. Suggest sweeping each tool's lower/upper (and pairwise corners) and warning on non-contact collision shapes below z=0 or on box-box penetration above OVERLAP_TOL. Pairs linked only through follower '*_level' pin links should count as adjacent.

The drive model (machine_env.py articulated/ackermann branches) has no speed-dependent steering or lateral-acceleration limit: full articulation at 8.6 m/s gives 1.64 g. A Drive.max_lateral_accel that clamps the articulation/steer target to atan-limited values at speed would let machines keep datasheet top speeds.

Follower and hydraulic-cylinder helpers are copy-pasted across machine files: _follower in 7 files, _cylinder_fit/_cylinder_pair variants in 7. spec.py should provide follower_joint() and hydraulic_cylinder() helpers. Multi-source linear followers (q = sum k_i*q_i + c) would also remove the 5 dummy '*_level' pin links this machine needs.

findings.description: Joint limits are written to the URDF rounded to 6 decimals, and many joints start exactly on a limit (`init == lower` or `init == upper`). Isaac Lab checks the default joint positions against the PhysX limits in float32 with a strict comparison. For revolute joints those limits have also been round-tripped through degrees in USD. mini_excavator `blade_joint` fails deterministically: init = blade_up = 0.3572842960 but the URDF says upper="0.357284", which is 2.96e-7 rad (about 10 float32 ulps) below init. Articulation initialisation raises ValueError, so HeavyMachineEnv('mini_excavator') cannot be built. showcase.py with default args loads every machine, so it dies on this one too. About 15 other revolute joints sit exactly on a nonzero limit and pass or fail depending on 1-ulp rounding: hydraulic_excavator/backhoe/wheeled_excavator/mini_excavator stick_joint, asphalt_paver screed_lift_joint (my float32 model says it fails by 1 ulp) and wing joints, concrete_mixer chute_lift, motor_grader ripper, telehandler and crane boom_luff, telescopic_boom_lift jib_joint (URDF lower -1.134464 is 1.4e-8 inside init), mini_excavator bucket_joint, and wheeled_excavator blade_joint.
findings.evidence: articulation.py:1920-1935 (_validate_cfg): `joint_pos_limits = self.root_physx_view.get_dof_limits()[0].to(self.device)`; `out_of_range = self._data.default_joint_pos[0] < joint_pos_limits[:, 0]`; `out_of_range |= self._data.default_joint_pos[0] > joint_pos_limits[:, 1]`; `... raise ValueError(msg)` with the message 'The following joints have default positions out of the limits'. The default comes from init_state.joint_pos (articulation.py:1684-1687), which machine_env.py:137 sets to `{j.name: j.init ...}`. The exception is caught in asset_base.py:316-320 (`builtins.ISAACLAB_CALLBACK_EXCEPTION = e`) and re-raised by SimulationContext.render() (simulation_context.py:597-601) inside DirectRLEnv.__init__ -> sim.reset(). urdf_builder.py:73-75 `_f(x) = f"{x:.6f}"...`; assets/heavy_machines/mini_excavator/mini_excavator.urdf:256 `<limit lower="-0.403446" upper="0.357284" .../>`; machines/mini_excavator.py:338 `lower=blade_down, upper=blade_up, init=blade_up`. Note that the env's own 'joints missing after URDF import' RuntimeError (machine_env.py:271) is also unreachable for the same reason: _process_cfg -> resolve_matching_names_values(strict) raises first.
findings.fix:
Pad the physical limits slightly outward and write them at full precision. The env already clamps tools (`_tool_lo/_tool_hi`) and followers to the exact spec limits, so the padding is never reached.

```python
# urdf_builder.py
LIMIT_PAD = 1e-4  # keeps every init strictly inside the float32 deg<->rad limits PhysX reports
...
        if jt.type in ("revolute", "prismatic"):
            out.append(f'    <limit lower="{jt.lower - LIMIT_PAD:.9g}" upper="{jt.upper + LIMIT_PAD:.9g}" '
                       f'effort="{_f(jt.effort)}" velocity="{_f(jt.velocity)}"/>')
```

Also add a rule to checks.validate that parses the generated URDF `<limit>` values and requires `lower < init < upper` with a margin of at least 1e-5, so this cannot come back. An env-only alternative is to nudge the defaults inward in articulation_cfg: `joint_pos={j.name: j.init if j.type == "continuous" else min(max(j.init, j.lower + 1e-4), j.upper - 1e-4) for j in spec.movable_joints}`.

findings.description: HeavyMachineEnvCfg leaves `num_rerenders_on_reset` at its default of 0. The observation returned by `env.reset()` therefore holds the previous render, as does the observation from the step that auto-resets a timed-out env. On the very first reset that previous render comes from the cameras' spawn pose at the env origin, z=0, inside the ground. _reset_idx moves the machine and calls _update_cameras, but no render happens before _get_observations reads `cam.data.output['rgb']`. As a result, scripted_demo's first frames and collect_machine.py's first frame of every episode (it calls `env._get_observations()` right after `env.reset()`, line 221) show the old scene. The forklift env sets this field for exactly this reason.
findings.evidence: direct_rl_env.py:313-331 reset(): `self._reset_idx(indices)`; `self.scene.write_data_to_sim()`; `self.sim.forward()`; `if self.sim.has_rtx_sensors() and self.cfg.num_rerenders_on_reset > 0: for _ in range(...): self.sim.render()`; `return self._get_observations(), self.extras`. The same applies to the step() auto-reset at lines 396-402. direct_rl_env_cfg.py:235-240: `num_rerenders_on_reset: int = 0` with the note 'When this is 0 ... Data collected from sensors after performing reset will be stale'. sensor_base.py:179-182: reset marks the sensor outdated, so data is re-read from the annotator, which still holds the last render. forklift_env.py:255-259: `num_rerenders_on_reset: int = 3  # ... Isaac Lab's default is 0 re-renders → stale images`.
findings.fix:
In HeavyMachineEnvCfg add:
```python
    # re-render after reset so the first frame of an episode shows the new spawn
    num_rerenders_on_reset: int = 3
```
I checked the rest of the step lifecycle against direct_rl_env.py:357-418 and it is consistent with the env: _pre_physics_step, then decimation x (_apply_action, scene.write_data_to_sim, sim.step(render=False), render when `_sim_step_counter % render_interval == 0`, scene.update), then _get_dones, _get_rewards, _reset_idx, _get_observations. _apply_action's `_substep` counter stays aligned with `_sim_step_counter`, so camera poses are set on the substep that is rendered.

findings.description: The line-up spacing comes from the init-pose bounding box plus a 4 m gap, but the animation sweeps every tool through its full range, swings continuous swing joints ±0.6 rad and drives steer/articulation joints to their limits. Nothing filters collisions between the separate fixed-base articulations or between them and the ground. Each step the script teleports joints into neighbours or the ground with a 1e6 PD hold, and PhysX then fights the contacts, which shows up as jitter or shaking. I reproduced the showcase sweep offline with K.bounding_box(spec, q, visual=False). Swept collision extents overlap the next machine for articulated_dump_truck (2.0 m), hydraulic_excavator (3.1 m), rigid_haul_truck (5.8 m), rough_terrain_crane (6.6 m), telescopic_boom_lift (4.3 m), wheel_loader (3.4 m), wheel_tractor_scraper (5.3 m) and telehandler (2.7 m). Tools also go below ground, e.g. the crane hook rope by 12.3 m, the hydraulic excavator by 3.9 m and the backhoe by 2.1 m.
findings.evidence: showcase.py:51-57: `lo, hi = K.bounding_box(spec)` (init pose only); `y = cursor - hi[1]`; `cursor = y + lo[1] - args_cli.gap`. Lines 72-82: tools use `mid + amp*sin(...)` across the full [lower, upper], continuous joints `0.6*sin`, steer/articulation `lim*sin`. Lines 88-90: `write_joint_state_to_sim(q, 0)`, `set_joint_position_target(q)`, `write_data_to_sim()` every step. machine_env.articulation_cfg gives no collision filtering, and ArticulationRootPropertiesCfg(enabled_self_collisions=False) only disables self-collision within one articulation.
findings.fix: (a) Space the machines by their swept collision extent. Put the pose formula in a helper `pose(spec, t)` keyed by joint name, with the phase taken from the spec's movable-joint index rather than the articulation index, so the same function can be sampled before sim.reset. Then use `lo_y = min(K.bounding_box(spec, pose(spec, t), visual=False)[0][1] for t in ts)` (and the same for hi_y) when placing machines. (b) Keep tools off the ground, for example by limiting the sweep of tools whose subtree's lowest point drops below 0 (use K.lowest_points). Alternatively, since the showcase is purely kinematic, turn collisions off: `cfg.spawn.collision_props = sim_utils.CollisionPropertiesCfg(collision_enabled=False)`. modify_collision_properties is @apply_nested (schemas.py:365) and is applied in _spawn_from_usd_file (from_files.py:333-334). It skips instanced collider prims, so check the log for its warning.

findings.description: None of the three scripts passes the AppLauncher `--device` argument into the simulation config. HeavyMachineEnvCfg.sim and showcase's SimulationCfg always use the default 'cuda:0', so `--device cpu` or `--device cuda:1` is silently ignored. Kit then runs on one device while physics and torch run on another. The same applies to scripted_demo.py:88 and showcase.py:44. make_env_cfg(**overrides) only sets top-level fields, so `sim.device` cannot be passed through it.
findings.evidence: app_launcher.py:300-306 adds `--device` (default from `_APPLAUNCHER_CFG_INFO['device'] = 'cuda:0'`). simulation_cfg.py:355: `device: str = "cuda:0"`. Isaac Lab tutorials pass it through explicitly, e.g. scripts/tutorials/01_assets/run_articulation.py: `sim_cfg = sim_utils.SimulationCfg(device=args_cli.device)`. The env's device is `self.sim.device` (direct_rl_env.py:274-276), which comes from cfg.sim.device.
findings.fix:
teleop_machine.py and scripted_demo.py:
```python
cfg = make_env_cfg(spec.name, enable_cameras=args_cli.enable_cameras, randomize_spawn=args_cli.random_spawn)
cfg.sim.device = args_cli.device
env = HeavyMachineEnv(cfg)
```
showcase.py:44: `sim = sim_utils.SimulationContext(sim_utils.SimulationCfg(dt=1 / 60, device=args_cli.device))`.

findings.description: `write_root_velocity_to_sim` sets the root's centre-of-mass velocity, but `_write_state` computes the velocity of the root link origin (`v·e + x_ref·w·n`). PhysX integrates that value as COM velocity for one substep before the pose is overwritten, so the rendered body is offset by (ω × r_com)·dt while turning. Root-link COM offsets from the origin are up to 4.07 m (concrete_mixer_truck), 3.87 m (rigid_haul_truck) and 1.13 m (wheel_loader). At 0.5 rad/s that is about 1-2 cm per frame, relative to cameras that are posed from the exact internal state. It does not crash, but it is the wrong API for the quantity being written.
findings.evidence: articulation.py:485-495: `def write_root_velocity_to_sim(...)`: 'NOTE: This sets the velocity of the root's center of mass rather than the roots frame.' It forwards to write_root_com_velocity_to_sim. articulation.py:527-559 `write_root_link_velocity_to_sim`: 'NOTE: This sets the velocity of the root's frame' and adds `ω × quat_apply(quat, com_pos_b)` before writing. Root COM offsets were computed with urdf_builder.link_inertia(spec.link(spec.root)).
findings.fix:
In _write_state replace
`self.robot.write_root_velocity_to_sim(vel, env_ids=env_ids)`
with
`self.robot.write_root_link_velocity_to_sim(vel, env_ids=env_ids)`.
It reads `data.root_link_quat_w`, which `write_root_pose_to_sim` on the previous line has just updated, so the call order is already correct. The env-ids handling is otherwise correct: write_root_link_pose_to_sim, write_joint_state_to_sim and set_joint_position_target all accept a long tensor for env_ids. `tensor != slice(None)` evaluates True, and with joint_ids=None no `[:, None]` broadcast happens (articulation.py:594-604, 1093-1101). Shapes (len(env_ids), 7 / 6 / J) match.

findings.description: UrdfFileCfg is used without `usd_dir`, so the URDF is re-imported into a new `/tmp/IsaacLab/usd_<date>_<time>_<rand>` directory on every launch. There is no lazy caching: every teleop, demo or collector start re-imports, showcase re-imports all ~18 machines, and /tmp fills up. `make_instanceable=True` has no effect, because UrdfConverter never reads it in this version (harmless, but misleading). The other converter settings are valid: JointDriveCfg(drive_type='force', target_type='position', gains=PDGainsCfg(stiffness=..., damping=...)) has its one required field (stiffness) set, fix_base (MISSING by default) is set, merge_fixed_joints=True only removes fixed joints and merged child bodies, and the movable-joint DOF names the env relies on are unchanged.
findings.evidence: asset_converter_base.py: 'When no output directory is defined, lazy conversion is deactivated and the generated USD file is stored in folder /tmp/IsaacLab/usd_{date}_{time}_{random}'; `if cfg.usd_dir is None: ... self._usd_dir = f"/tmp/IsaacLab/usd_{time_tag}_{random.randrange(10000)}"`. urdf_converter.py `_get_urdf_import_config` sets density, convex_decomp, collision_from_visuals, merge_fixed_joints/merge_fixed_ignore_inertia, fix_base, self_collision, parse_mimic and replace_cylinders, and never touches make_instanceable. grep shows `make_instanceable` is only used in mesh_converter.py:167. urdf_converter_cfg.py: `stiffness: ... = MISSING`, `fix_base: bool = MISSING`.
findings.fix:
```python
urdf_path, _ = write_assets(spec)
spawn=sim_utils.UrdfFileCfg(
    asset_path=urdf_path,
    usd_dir=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(urdf_path), "usd_fixed" if fix_base else "usd"),
    fix_base=fix_base, merge_fixed_joints=True, ...)
```
The hash covers the cfg and the URDF bytes (asset_converter_base._config_to_hash), so an edited spec still triggers a re-import. Remove `make_instanceable=True`, or leave it with a comment that UrdfConverter ignores it.

The back-wall box (1.83 m wide, rear face only 0.04 m ahead of the coupler pin) is directly in front of the arm front-leg boxes (y 0.66–0.80), and the legs lean back only 13.7° from vertical at the pin. Make the dark coupler plate span the gap between the pin and the back wall (the tilt lugs stay on the coupler). Then add a local check (or a test) that sweeps bucket_joint over [BUCKET_LO, BUCKET_HI] and asserts lift_arm/bucket box penetration ≤ 0.03 m. issues.description: The tilt-cylinder layout goes through dead centre in the middle of the bucket range. During one dump from carry, the rod visibly retracts and then re-extends, which a real hydraulic cylinder cannot do. Near q≈-0.6 the line of action passes 1.7 cm from the hinge pin, so this cylinder could not drive the bucket through that point. issues.description: Dumping the bucket at carry height drives it deep into the ground, and the scripted task generator will do this often. Since the env writes root and joint states every substep, Isaac will show the bucket sunk into the ground plane while PhysX fights the penetration. core_issues: checks.py self-overlap skips every parent-child pair and only tests the init pose. That hid a 0.12 m box-box penetration between lift_arm and bucket here, which also grows across the tool range. Also sample each tool joint at lower/init/upper (with followers resolved) and warn on overlaps above OVERLAP_TOL.

tasks.py sample_goals picks loader bucket targets uniformly regardless of lift height, so collected episodes routinely sink the bucket 0.3–1.0 m into the ground. At init lift, below-ground fractions of the bucket range: skid_steer_loader 65%, compact_track_loader 74%, wheel_loader 55%, backhoe_loader 41%. test_env_logic.test_turn_left_increases_yaw runs 90 control steps (3 s) and checks the atan2-wrapped env._yaw, so any skid machine with max_yaw_rate > π/3 ≈ 1.047 rad/s fails spuriously. Fix: accumulate unwrapped yaw in the test, or run fewer steps (e.g. 30).

Linear followers cannot represent two-pin hydraulic cylinders, and at least 7 machine files (articulated_dump_truck, asphalt_paver, backhoe_loader, bulldozer, compact_track_loader, mini_excavator, skid_steer_loader) each carry their own _rot/_cylinder_fit/_minimax_fit copy. findings.description: The root velocity goes to the wrong Isaac Lab API. `write_root_velocity_to_sim` sets the root's centre-of-mass velocity. But `vel` (lines 429-433) is the velocity of the root-link origin, `v*e - x_ref*w*n`. During each physics substep PhysX moves the COM at the origin's velocity and rotates the body about the COM, so the origin lands off by `w x r_com * dt`.
findings.evidence: Isaac Lab source in the repo: articulation.py:485-495 says `write_root_velocity_to_sim` -> `write_root_com_velocity_to_sim` ("sets the velocity of the root's center of mass rather than the roots frame"). articulation.py:527-559 `write_root_link_velocity_to_sim` adds `w x (R*com_b)`. Offset of the merged root-body COM from the root origin (urdf_builder.link_inertia over the root plus its fixed children): concrete_mixer_truck +4.07 m, rigid_haul_truck +3.86 m, motor_grader +1.50 m, wheel_loader +1.13 m, articulated_dump_truck -0.60 m. Resulting COM-velocity error \|w\|*\|r_com\|: 2.0 m/s for the mixer at w=0.5 rad/s, and 13.3 m/s at its maximum kinematic yaw rate of 3.27 rad/s. That is 1.7 cm of lateral pose error per substep at w=0.5. The error is not cumulative because the pose is rewritten each substep, but it is what gets rendered (see the next finding).
findings.fix: Line 435: `self.robot.write_root_link_velocity_to_sim(vel, env_ids=env_ids)`. If the next finding's preferred fix (write zero velocities) is adopted, this change is no longer needed.

findings.description: The Odometry twist is wrong in two ways. (1) It reports `speed*(cos yaw, sin yaw)` as the root's linear velocity. `speed` is the velocity of the reference axle (the fixed axle, or the front axle for articulated machines), not of the root origin. Whenever x_ref != 0 the root origin has an extra `-x_ref*w*n` term. (2) It is written in the world frame, but nav_msgs/Odometry defines the twist in child_frame_id (the root body frame).
findings.evidence: Finite-difference velocity of the root origin compared with the odom `lin`, after 3 s at drive=0.5, turn=+1, start yaw 1.0: wheel_loader (x_ref=+1.675, w=0.937) true (-4.42,+1.19) vs odom (-4.28,-0.39), error 1.59 m/s. rough_terrain_crane (x_ref=-1.675, w=1.016) error 1.68 m/s. soil_compactor 0.46 m/s. telescopic_boom_lift 0.25 m/s. Each error equals \|x_ref*w\|.
findings.fix: In body frame (correct for nav_msgs/Odometry with child_frame_id=root): `lin = (state[3], -env._x_ref * state[4], 0.0)`. If a world-frame vector is wanted instead: `c, s = cos(yaw), sin(yaw); lin = (v*c + x_ref*w*s, v*s - x_ref*w*c, 0.0)`. Better still, expose `x_ref` (or the root velocity) as a public env attribute.

findings.description: Every steer joint gets the virtual centre-wheel rate (`step/dt`) as its velocity. Under Ackermann geometry the inner and outer wheels turn at different rates. These wrong velocities are written to PhysX and published as /joint_states velocity, since the collector reads `env._qd`.
findings.evidence: Finite difference of the written angle compared with the reported qd while steering from 0 to full lock: rigid_haul_truck front_left 0.363 rad/s actual vs 0.250 reported; front_right 0.181 vs 0.250. telescopic_boom_lift (rear steer) rear_left -0.511 vs -0.350; rear_right -0.250 vs -0.350. The error is up to 46%.
findings.fix: Lines 355-356: `prev = self._q[:, self._steer_ids].clone(); self._q[:, self._steer_ids] = ang; qd[:, self._steer_ids] = (ang - prev) / dt`.

findings.description: Tool qd is set to 0 whenever the clamped position touches a limit, including the substep in which the joint actually moved part of the way to that limit. For non-wrapping joints, qd should be the real displacement divided by dt.
findings.evidence: hydraulic_excavator, all tools at +1: on the substep where the boom reaches its upper limit, the finite difference is +0.1997 rad/s but the reported qd is 0.0.
findings.fix: `q_old = self._q[:, self._tool_ids]` (line 395, before the update); then `qd[:, self._tool_ids] = torch.where(self._tool_wrap, rate, (q - q_old) / dt)`. The `hit` variable can be dropped.

findings.description: The rendered machine runs one physics substep ahead of its own cameras. `_apply_action` integrates to t+dt, writes pose(t+dt) together with non-zero root and joint velocities, and places the cameras at the internal pose(t+dt). DirectRLEnv.step then calls `sim.step()`, so PhysX advances the body by vel*dt, and `sim.render()` runs only after that. The machine is therefore drawn at about t+2dt while the cameras sit at t+dt. Separately, the written joint velocities fight the PD drive, whose velocity target is 0: damping of 1e4*qd puts reaction torques on the chassis.
findings.evidence: Order is from direct_rl_env.py:373-384 (`_apply_action` -> `write_data_to_sim` -> `sim.step` -> `render` every 4th substep). Cameras are set at machine_env.py:410-411 on that same 4th substep. Offset between camera and body is v_max*dt (dt=1/120): concrete_mixer 0.183 m, wheel_tractor_scraper 0.128 m, rigid_haul_truck 0.125 m, ADT 0.122 m, motor_grader 0.104 m. Yaw lead w_max*dt is up to 1.67 deg (backhoe). A cab camera therefore sees the hood or bucket shifted forward in proportion to the commanded speed. Wheel damping example: 4 wheels x 1e4 x 15 rad/s = 6e5 N*m. Note that forklift_env.py:1049-1084 avoids this by reading back the solver pose.
findings.fix: Treat the pose as authoritative and stop PhysX from advancing it. In `_write_state`: `zero6 = torch.zeros(pose.shape[0], 6, device=self.device); self.robot.write_root_velocity_to_sim(zero6, env_ids=env_ids); self.robot.write_joint_state_to_sim(self._q[ids], torch.zeros_like(self._q[ids]), env_ids=env_ids)`. Keep `self._qd` for observations and bags; the props are static, so the velocities serve no purpose. Alternative: write the pre-integration pose(t) with `write_root_link_velocity_to_sim` and `set_joint_velocity_target(self._qd)`, then integrate, so the PhysX step lands on the state the cameras use.

findings.description: Camera images are stale or duplicated. `camera_update_hz=15` with 30 Hz control means an image is refreshed only on some control steps. Isaac Lab's float32 sensor timestamp with its 1e-6 tolerance (sensor_base.py:187) makes the refresh slip to every 3rd step after a few seconds. Also, HeavyMachineEnvCfg leaves `num_rerenders_on_reset=0`, so after `env.reset()` the camera data still holds the previous episode's last render: Camera.reset only marks the buffer outdated, and `_update_buffers_impl` reads whatever was rendered last.
findings.evidence: Simulating the SensorBase update rule (float32, dt=1/120, period=1/15, data read once per control step): refreshes at steps 0,2,4,... but the first 3-step gap appears at step 123 (4.1 s). Over 300 s, gaps are {2: 540, 3: 2639}, so only 35% of steps get a fresh image (~10.6 Hz). collect_machine.py records LeRobot at 30 fps every step (lines 263-293), so 65% of frames repeat an older image under a newer state/action. After reset: step 0 is stale (no render), and at step 1 the timestamp is 0.033 < 0.0667, so steps 0 and 1 of every episode show the previous episode's final frame.
findings.fix: In `_setup_scene`'s CameraCfg use `update_period=0.0` (refresh on every read, i.e. every control step; the collector already subsamples via `image_period`). Do not use 1/30, because the float32 drift then skips frames too. Add `num_rerenders_on_reset: int = 1` to HeavyMachineEnvCfg (use 2-3 if RTX accumulation needs it) so the frames after a reset show the new spawn.

findings.description: The "turn left N degrees" goal does not produce N degrees of heading change. It completes as soon as the root yaw reaches N while the steering or articulation is still at full lock. The next goal then unwinds the steering at the rate limit, often at full drive speed, which keeps turning. For articulated machines the measured yaw is the front frame's, which includes the articulation "kick" (-l_r*g_dot/(l_f*cos g + l_r)); that kick reverses when steering re-centres, and the cab (on the rear frame for wheel_loader and soil_compactor) has barely turned at completion. This contradicts the tasks.py claim that language, actions and outcome agree.
findings.evidence: Goal [turn +N, drive 4 m], then let the steering settle. Final heading at gamma/delta=0: rigid_haul_truck 30->46.9 deg, 90->117.3 deg. wheel_loader 30->37.8, 90->109.7. soil_compactor 30->35.4, 90->100.2. wheel_tractor_scraper 30->18.6, 90->66.2. ADT 30->27.9. hydraulic_excavator (skid) 30->28.6 (correct). When wheel_loader's "turn left 30" is judged done, the front yaw is 28.3 deg but the cab/rear frame yaw is 5.6 deg (soil_compactor: -0.6 deg).
findings.fix: In the turn branch, (a) release the turn command early: set a[1]=0 once the remaining yaw is at or below the predicted unwind yaw. For Ackermann that is `v*(-ln cos(delta))/(L*steer_rate)` (exact for a linear ramp). For articulated machines, integrate the env's omega_f formula numerically over the gamma ramp back to 0, about 20 steps. (b) Call `_advance()` only when `abs(state[5]) < 0.01` and the heading error is <= 2 deg. Hold drive at 0.5 during the unwind so the next goal does not unwind at full speed.

findings.description: The spawn region overlaps the prop annulus, and props cannot stop the machine. The pose is overwritten every substep and the props are static colliders, so the machine passes straight through dirt piles and boulders. The module docstring (lines 28-30) says "the ground plane and props still collide with it", which misleads. Dirt piles have radius up to 4 m and props_inner_radius is 14 m, so props can reach within 10 m of the origin, while the spawn corner is at hypot(8,8)=11.3 m, before adding machine half-length or scripted travel.
findings.evidence: 40 seeded scripted episodes per machine, with an oriented bounding box of the machine tested against prop footprints replicated from `_spawn_site_props` (props_seed=0). Overlap at spawn / at any time: articulated_dump_truck 1/40 and 9/40; wheel_tractor_scraper 2/40 and 5/40; wheel_loader 0/40 and 3/40; hydraulic_excavator 0/40 and 0/40.
findings.fix: Either make the geometry consistent, i.e. `props_inner_radius - 4.0 >= hypot(spawn half-extent) + envelope_L/2 + goals_max*6.0` (for example a smaller spawn region and a larger annulus), or have the collector reject or re-sample episodes whose swept footprint hits a prop (the layout is deterministic from props_seed). Correct the docstring: props are visual and static only, and the machine does not respond to them.

findings.description: Every `wheel`-role joint spins at v/r. In a turn the inner, outer, rear-frame and steered wheels all roll at different ground speeds, so the wheels touching the ground visibly slip, and those joint velocities are also written to PhysX. Skid machines already use a per-side speed; wheeled machines do not.
findings.evidence: Steady-state longitudinal slip at the contact point (finite difference of the bottom material point via FK): wheel_loader full lock at 4.3 m/s gives +/-1.03 m/s on every wheel. rigid_haul_truck delta=0.52 at 4.5 m/s gives front_right +1.77, rear_outer +/-1.31, rear_inner +/-0.83 m/s. Tracked sprockets slip 0.001 m/s longitudinally (correct).
findings.fix: In `_build_joint_maps`, precompute for each rolling joint: (x_i, y_i) from FK, the column of its parent steer joint (or -1), whether it is in the articulation child subtree, and its y in the rear frame. Then: unsteered wheel on the root: `sp = v - w*y_i`. Steered wheel: `sp = (v - w*y_i)*cos(phi) + w*(x_i - x_ref)*sin(phi)`. Articulated rear wheel: `v_r = v*cos(g) - d.front_length*w*sin(g); sp = v_r - (w + g_dot)*y_i`. For skid machines this reproduces v -/+ w*W/2 from the actual y positions.

findings.description: The docs say "turn > 0 always means turn left (CCW)" (also machine_env.py:12). In reverse, Ackermann and articulated machines yaw clockwise for turn=+1 (car steering-wheel semantics), while skid machines stay CCW. The same action therefore means opposite yaw directions across machine types, which matters for a cross-machine dataset and for teleop.
findings.evidence: drive=-0.5, turn=+1 for 3 s: hydraulic_excavator (skid) yaw +1.500 rad; backhoe_loader -1.922; wheel_loader -1.126; telescopic_boom_lift -0.447.
findings.fix: Correct the docs: "turn>0 steers left: CCW when moving forward; wheeled (ackermann/articulated) machines yaw CW when reversing, skid machines always CCW." Alternatively make the semantics uniform, but the doc fix is the minimal change.

findings.description: Follower handling is inconsistent but currently harmless. The env clamps the follower to its limits, while `kinematics.resolve_followers` (kinematics.py:160) does not clamp. `link_transforms`, which camera FK uses, re-resolves followers and would overwrite the env's clamped value. The follower's qd also stays `k*qd_src` while it is clamped.
findings.evidence: For all followers in all 18 machines, k*[src.lower, src.upper]+c stays within the follower's limits, so the clamp never engages today. One example: telescopic_boom_lift's front camera sits downstream of the platform_level/jib_level followers, so a future clamp would desynchronise that camera.
findings.fix: kinematics.py:160: `val = k*src+c; out[jt.name] = val if jt.type == 'continuous' else min(max(val, jt.lower), jt.upper)`. In the env: `val = k*q_src + c0; self._q[:, idx] = val.clamp(lo, hi); qd[:, idx] = torch.where((val < lo) \| (val > hi), 0.0, k*qd[:, src])`. Alternatively add a checks.py error when a follower's mapped range exceeds its limits.

findings.description: The core kinematics were verified correct, but the existing tests do not lock them in. They check only the yaw sign and wheel ordering, not the no-slip constraints. Items verified: skid track speeds v -/+ w*W/2; Ackermann w = s*v*tan(delta)/L and per-wheel s*atan(L/(R_icr - y)), including rear steer; root velocity v*e - x_ref*w*n; the articulated yaw rate -(v sin g + l_r g_dot)/(l_f cos g + l_r) and its sign; x_ref = hinge_x + front_length as the front-axle no-slip point for the ROOT=front frame (correct for all 3 articulated machines: ADT and scraper x_ref=0.000 = front wheel x, wheel_loader 1.675, soil_compactor 1.400); midpoint yaw integration (relative error (w*dt)^2/24); wrapping; return-to-centre; +q about +y rolls forward; camera composition `base @ FK @ mount` with (w,x,y,z) in the 'world' convention; env_origins; partial reset; multi-env.
findings.evidence: Lateral (no-slip) velocity from finite differences while turning at 2-6 m/s: fixed axle <= 1.5e-4 m/s; steered kingpins <= 9.6e-3 m/s (FD error during the steer ramp); articulated front axle <= 4.6e-3 and rear axle <= 1.0e-2 m/s. Steady turning radius matches theory to 1e-4 m (ADT 7.5775 vs 7.5774; scraper 10.6614 vs 10.6614; boom-lift rear steer 4.1987 vs 4.1985). Quaternion round trip max error 8.9e-16 over 20,000 random rotations plus 180 deg cases. Camera heading/pitch exact (+1.000 / +0.350 rad). 3-env vs 1-env results differ by <= 1.5e-5 (float32). Skid contact-patch centre at root x = 0.00 for all 6 skid machines. The existing 9 tests pass (127 s).
findings.fix: Add a test that runs `_apply_action` substeps, finite-differences `robot.root_pose`, and asserts: lateral velocity of (fixed_axle_x, 0) < 1e-2*v for Ackermann; front axle and rear axle (hinge + Rz(g)(-l_r, 0), heading yaw+g) < 2e-2*v for articulated; each steered kingpin's velocity direction == yaw + q_steer. Also optionally derive the articulated x_ref from the mean x of front-frame rolling joints instead of spec.front_length, since checks.py allows 0.15 m slack.

result.summary:
