No allowed_overlaps were needed. The livery uses DEFAULT_MATERIALS, since CAT and Volvo ADTs are both yellow. No tailgate: it is optional on both trucks, so I kept the standard open tail chute.
result.datasheet:
Datasheet numbers and assumptions (CAT 730 / Volvo A30G class, rounded; also listed in the module docstring):
- Operating mass (empty) 23.5 t; rated payload 28 t; heaped body 17.5 m³; 6x6 with three axles.
- Tyres 23.5R25: outer diameter 1.61 m (rolling radius 0.805 m), section 0.60 m.
- Gauge 2.32 m; width over tyres 2.92 m; body width about 2.93 m.
- Overall length 10.4 m (A30G 10.3 m, CAT 730 about 10.5 m).
- Height over cab ROPS/beacon 3.43–3.44 m; loading height (body top rail) about 3.0 m.
- Front axle to bumper 1.50 m; front axle to hitch 2.15 m; hitch to first bogie axle 3.00 m; bogie axle spacing 1.67 m; front axle to tandem centre 5.99 m.
- Ground clearance 0.50 m at the axle differentials.
- Articulation ±45° (±0.785 rad), lock-to-lock about 4.5 s (0.35 rad/s); model outer turning radius about 9.0 m.
- Tipping angle 70° (1.22 rad), tipping time 12 s (0.10 rad/s).
- Height with body raised: about 6.5 m for the real class; the model is 6.9 m including the canopy lip.
- Top speed 53 km/h (14.7 m/s); reverse about 15 km/h (4.2 m/s).
- Body pivot 0.88 m behind the last axle at 1.55 m above ground; body runs from 1.2 m behind the pivot to 4.85 m ahead of it (plus a 0.37 m canopy lip).
- Hoist cylinders: two single-stage cylinders, base just behind the hitch (0.95 m above ground), eye under the body 2.2 m ahead of the pivot; pin distance 2.8 m retracted to 5.1 m extended.
- Assumed mass split: front tractor 10.2 t, rear frame 4.2 t, body 4.8 t, six tyre-and-rim assemblies at 0.65 t each, hoist cylinders 0.36 t.
remaining_warnings: No checker warnings (0 errors, 0 warnings).

Model width is 2.97 m against the 2.92 m envelope (+1.7%). The extra is only the shared wheel_link spoke bar, which sticks out 2.4 cm past each tyre face; the tyres and body themselves are 2.92-2.93 m.

Height with the body raised is 6.9 m in the model, about 6.5 m on the real class. The 70° tip angle and the body length are datasheet values, and the pivot cannot move forward without the body tail hitting the rear tyres, so I left it and documented it in the docstring.

Hoist cylinders are cosmetic. Each one stays straight and pinned to the rear frame, but its rod eye slides up to about 0.6 m along a dark bracket under the body (within about ±0.1 m of the underside) while tipping. Followers can only produce link angles that are linear in the source joint, and the true pin-to-pin angle deviates by up to ±4° over a 70° tip. I chose this over the alternative of two halves pinned at both ends, which left the halves 0.2-0.3 m out of line. The cameras never see the hoist.

The matplotlib previews sometimes draw the long hoist cylinders on top of nearer tyres. That is a draw-order (painter's sorting) artefact of the preview renderer, not geometry; the real clearance to the tyres is at least 8 cm.
core_issues: Glass is probably opaque in Isaac (not run there; inferred from the URDF): the 'glass' material has alpha 1.0 and urdf_builder.py writes plain opaque colours with no transparency. A camera behind a windscreen would then see a solid blue pane instead of the scene. wheeled_excavator's front camera is 0.2 m behind its windscreen, well past the 0.1 m near clip, so it would likely see the pane. hydraulic_excavator's is 0.09 m behind and pitched 0.35 rad, so the lower part of its image likely shows the pane. I avoided this by putting the ADT front camera just ahead of the windscreen. A fix would be a translucent glass material in urdf_builder, or a documented rule that cab cameras sit in front of the glass.

Follower joints are linear only (q = k*q_src + c), so in a planar chain a follower link's angle is always linear in the source. Two-pin hydraulic cylinders over a large stroke (70° body tip, boom lifts, crane luffing) therefore cannot stay collinear and pinned at both ends. My workaround is in the ADT file (straight barrel with a sliding rod, eye on a bracket). Adding a nonlinear follower to spec.py, kinematics.resolve_followers and machine_env (e.g. 'aim this link at a point on another link', or polynomial coefficients) would fix it for every machine.

Minor: the header comment that urdf_builder.build_urdf writes into every URDF says the file is generated by 'scripts/heavy_machines/generate.py'. That script does not exist; check_machine.py writes the files.

Minor: render.py draws shapes in order of each shape's mean depth, so long thin shapes such as hoist cylinders can appear over nearer tyres in the side and 3-D previews. This affects the preview images only.
Not mine: test_machines.py fails test_committed_assets_in_sync for motor_grader because its assets have not been generated yet. That is presumably another agent's in-progress machine.

issues.description: Steered front tyres and mudguards pass through the folded stabiliser pads and legs, the right frame rail and the boom base. Every turn goal commands turn=±1, which is full lock, so this happens in essentially every episode that turns.
issues.evidence: OBB overlap check (checks._obb / obb_penetration) at ackermann_wheel_angles(±0.65): the outer tyre is 0.257 m into the stabiliser pad box at (3.20, ±0.55, agl 0.455), and already 0.127 m at virtual steer 0.3. At full right lock the front_right_wheel is 0.165 m into the right frame rail (box at y = BOOM_Y-0.33 = -0.45, x -1.10..3.05) and 0.045-0.055 m into the boom_base side plate. Cause: the tyre's plan-view sweep radius about its steer axis (2.75, ±0.97) is sqrt(0.655²+0.25²) = 0.70 m, but the pads sit 0.41 m from it. The stabiliser beam at x = 3.20 is inside the straight-ahead tyre's x span (front edge 3.405). At 46.1° the inner tyre's rear-inner corner reaches y = ±0.325, which the right rail at -0.45 blocks. Corrected top-view render at full lock shows the overlap. In the front-camera render at full right lock, the left mudguard swings into the yellow stabiliser leg in the middle of the image.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the stabiliser group (beam, legs, pads, rams in _chassis_frame) forward to x ≈ 3.55-3.60 so the pads start at x ≥ 3.40. It stays behind the boom head and carriage in the travel pose and inside the 7.56 m envelope; recheck clearance under the head. End the frame rails at x ≈ 2.0 and use a narrow front nose (|y| ≤ 0.27, symmetric about y = 0) for the axle and stabiliser mount, or lower max_steer. Re-run the overlap check at ±max_steer until it is clean.

issues.description: The carriage hitch plate and bottom bar cut into the boom-head drop-nose box when tilting back near the travel pose and when tilting forward at high luff. Because the tilt range is measured from level, the carriage can rotate 171° relative to the boom (-141° to +30°), more than a real carriage.
issues.evidence: Overlap grid (luff × telescope × tilt): boom_fly head box (center (5.3, 0, -0.12) in the fly frame) vs carriage hitch plate box(0.10, 0.50, 0.80) overlap by 0.088 m at fork_tilt +0.40 and luff -0.127 (any extension), 0.046 m at luff 0, and 0.132 m / 0.235 m at fork_tilt -1.25 with luff 1.0 / 1.209. Zoomed side renders show the plate inside the dark head box at travel with tilt +0.40, and the carriage frame buried in the head at max luff with tilt -1.25.
issues.suggested_fix: Shorten the dark head box to end about 0.05 m behind the carriage pin and give it a rounded nose (a cylinder about y at the pin, r ≤ 0.25). Replace the central 0.50 m hitch plate with two narrow plates outboard of the head's ±0.20 m, like the pivot lugs at ±0.24. Alternatively narrow the tilt range. Then re-run the overlap check over the luff × tilt grid.

issues.description: Scripted tasks drive the forks and boom well below the ground. Telescope goals ≥30% from the travel pose bury the carriage 0.30-1.29 m. The only fork-tilt goals possible from init (forward to ≤49%) put the fork tips at least 0.49 m underground.
issues.evidence: FK: at luff_lo with full extension the pin is at -0.67 m and the carriage at -1.29 m above ground (agl). At init with tilt -1.25 the carriage is at -1.01 agl. init fork_tilt = 79% of range, and sample_goals requires a ≥30% change, so the first tilt goal is always ≤49% (q ≤ -0.44), giving tips ≈ -0.49 agl. Running tasks.sample_goals for 400 episodes: 271 have carriage or boom >5 cm below grade at a goal end state (median -1.00 m, worst -2.41 m). telescopic_boom_lift scores 0/150, so a machine-level design can avoid this.
issues.suggested_fix: Mainly a core fix (see core_issues): make the goal sampler reject goal states that put collision shapes below ground. Machine option: set the luff lower limit and init to about -0.05 rad. Level forks then never go below grade at full extension, and the travel pose carries the forks at about 0.55 m, a realistic carry height but higher than the brief's 'just above the ground'. Otherwise state the limitation in notes.

issues.description: The front (operator) camera loses the forks above about half the luff range, so most lift goals ('raise the boom luff to 60-100%') leave the forks out of the main view.
issues.evidence: Projected the fork midpoint into the front camera (horizontal FOV 92.7°, half 46.3°, square image). At pitch 0.18 the forks are in view only up to luff ≈ 0.55 rad (elevation +51° retracted at 0.60 rad, +69° at 0.80 rad). At pitch 0.0 they stay in view up to about 0.70 rad, and the travel-pose forks are still visible at -30°. In my render of the mid pose (luff 0.45, about 3 m total extension) the carriage is already at the top edge, contradicting 'sees the carriage at mid-height lifts'.
issues.suggested_fix: Set the front camera pitch to about 0.0 (or -0.05) so near-ground fork work and mid-height lifts both stay in frame. Keep yaw -0.15.

issues.description: Direction words with underscores appear verbatim in the generated language instructions.
issues.evidence: tasks.sample_goals output for this machine includes 'tilt_back the fork tilt to …%' and 'tilt_forward the fork tilt to …%'. The task template is f"{word} the {label}", and only the label has its underscores replaced.

The carriage pin at luff 0.5 and full extension is identical: (13.5558, -0.12, 8.8689).

issues.description: The front-right mudguard fills roughly the lower-left quarter of the right camera image in every pose.
issues.evidence: Approximate pinhole render of the right camera at (1.98, -1.09, 1.88 m above ground), yaw -0.75: the mudguard on the knuckle is 0.4-1.1 m away and within 0.45-0.63 rad of the optical axis.

core_issues: tasks.sample_goals ignores the ground: tool targets are sampled with no ground check. Class values for the Bobcat S650 / CAT 262D3, rounded. These are from recall, not looked up from a datasheet, and are also listed in the module docstring:

- Tyres 12-16.5: diameter 0.84 m, section 0.31 m, 16.5 in rim.
- Wheelbase 1.16 m; tread 1.45 m; width over tyres 1.76 m.
- Bucket 72 in: 1.83 m wide, about 0.40 m³ heaped. Overall width uses the bucket.
- Length with the bucket on the ground 3.45 m (model 3.47 m at lift q=0, 3.61 m in the carry pose); length without attachment about 2.8 m (model about 2.75 m).
- Height to top of cab 2.06 m; ground clearance 0.20 m.
- Arm pivot height about 1.54 m; hinge-pin height at max lift 3.13 m (matched exactly).
- Dump height about 2.45 m (model 2.52 m); dump reach about 0.6 m (model 0.62 m).
- Dump angle at max height 42° (model 41°); rollback 30° at the ground (model 31.5°) and 97° at full height (model 97°).
- Raise time about 3.3 s (0.34 rad/s over 1.13 rad); dump about 2 s (0.9 rad/s).
- Travel 11.9 km/h (3.3 m/s).
- Spin turn 1.0–1.2 rad/s; the model uses 1.0 rad/s because of the shared-test limit described in core_issues.

Assumptions:
- Single-pin radial lift path. The real S650 / 262D3 vertical-lift linkage is a closed loop URDF cannot express; the pin heights and the bucket angles at both ends match.
- Livery is CAT yellow (DEFAULT_MATERIALS), so no custom materials.
- Init pose = carry/travel pose: lift 0.06 rad, bucket 0.40 rad.
remaining_warnings: tool bucket: directions 'curl'/'dump' not auto-verifiable. Justified: the checker's vocabulary has no word for bucket curl, same as the reference hydraulic_excavator. I verified the sign visually in skid_steer_loader_sweeps.png: blue (+0.55) rolls the cutting edge back and up, and red (-1.85) dumps the bucket nose-down. The axis is (0,-1,0) with bucket +x toward the cutting edge, so +q raises the edge.
core_issues: test_env_logic.py test_turn_left_increases_yaw runs 90 control steps (3 s) with turn=+1 and then checks yaw > 0.05. env._yaw is wrapped with atan2, so any skid machine with max_yaw_rate above π/3 ≈ 1.047 rad/s wraps past π and fails: at the requested 1.2 rad/s yaw reached 3.6 rad and wrapped to -2.68. I worked around it by using max_yaw_rate=1.0 (360° spin in 6.3 s, still realistic). Suggested fix: integrate yaw unwrapped in the test, or shorten the run to fewer steps.

render.py _draw_ortho uses the wrong painter's order for the 'top' and 'front' panels: both use sgn=-1, so lower and rearmost shapes are drawn last. The 'top' panel is therefore really a view from below, and the 'front' panel is a view from behind; my 'front' panel shows the rear grille and tail lights. This misleads visual review for every machine. Fix: use sgn=+1 for 'top' (depth=z) and 'front' (depth=x). For my own review I used a scratch renderer with the correct order.

Glass material is opaque (alpha 1.0, exported as URDF rgba), so any camera behind a glass pane would likely see the pane in Isaac. The reference hydraulic_excavator's front camera sits inside its cab box, behind the windscreen pane at x≈1.26, so it is probably blinded in Isaac (not verified in Isaac Sim). I placed my front camera just ahead of the front door glass to avoid this. Suggest documenting this camera-placement rule in spec.py, or making glass translucent or visual-optional for camera paths.

Followers are linear (q = k*q_src + c), so two-pin hydraulic cylinders with large swing can only be approximated; the 137° bucket tilt range is the hard case. My workaround: pin the barrel at its base and the rod at its eye, and fit only their shared direction (minimax), which keeps them within 3.7 cm of coaxial. A built-in 'aim at a point on another link' follower would make cylinders exact for every machine.

result.summary:
The bulldozer (DOZ, dozing) is built, modelled on a 20 t CAT D6 / Komatsu D65EX-class crawler dozer. `check_machine.py bulldozer` prints OK with 0 errors and 1 justified warning, and has written `assets/heavy_machines/bulldozer/bulldozer.urdf` and `.json`. Both test suites pass for the bulldozer. The only failure is `test_committed_assets_in_sync` for `soil_compactor`, another agent's in-progress machine.

**Dimensions and mass**
- Size in the init (transport) pose is 6.64 x 3.43 x 3.20 m against an envelope of 6.60 x 3.42 x 3.20 m, under 1% off.
- Mass is 20,390 kg against an operating mass of 20,500 kg. Split: tractor 14.0 t, blade 2.6 t, push arms 2 x 650 kg, lift frame 120 kg, lift cylinders 220 + 120 kg, ripper parts 1.73 t, sprockets 2 x 150 kg.
- Root height is 0.33 m.
- The undercarriage is high-drive steel tracks: front and rear idlers on the ground, elevated sprocket under the rear of the cab.
- Track gauge 1.88 m, 0.56 m shoes, 2.8 m of track on the ground, 0.40 m ground clearance.

**Drive**
- Skid steer: 2.8 m/s forward, 3.3 m/s reverse, 0.5 rad/s yaw, track width 1.88 m.
- The sprockets are the rolling elements (roll_left / roll_right, radius 0.33 m).

**Tools**
- **blade_lift** (+1 = raise): range -0.161 to +0.359 rad, init +0.125, 0.18 rad/s. The push arms pivot on trunnions on the track roller frames, outboard of the tracks. The cutting edge goes from 0.50 m below grade (0.54 m at the wing tips) to 1.12 m above ground, and sits 0.38 m up at init.
- **blade_tilt** (+1 = tilt_left, -1 = tilt_right): range ±0.20 rad, 0.15 rad/s, giving a 0.66 m height difference between the blade corners.
  - tilt_left lowers the left (+y) end, following the operator convention (joystick left on CAT / Komatsu).
  - I confirmed the sign in the front panels of the pose render, the large 3D views, and a pinhole preview of the three cameras.
  - Both push arms follow the tilt (one up, one down, k = ∓0.502) so their ball joints stay on the blade.
- **ripper** (+1 = raise): range -0.545 to +0.555 rad, init at the upper limit, 0.30 rad/s. It is a parallelogram linkage: the tool beam follows with k = -1 so the shank stays vertical, and the upper link with k = +1. The shank tip goes from 0.59 m below grade to 0.56 m above ground.

**Visual detail**
- Semi-U blade: 3.42 x 1.42 m curved moldboard, wings swept forward 24°, end plates, steel cutting edge and end bits, back box beams and ribs.
- Push arms outboard of the tracks, a tilt cylinder on the right and a brace on the left.
- Engine hood sloping down toward the radiator, with louvres, exhaust stack and pre-cleaner. Radiator guard with grille and lamps.
- Fenders with handrails, centred ROPS cab with glass panes, roof work lights, fuel tank with tail lights.
- Track rollers, idler discs, a sprocket disc with spokes so the spin is visible, and grouser bars on the upper track run.
- The hydraulic cylinders (blade lift and ripper) are visual-only followers. Their angles are fitted linearly to the tool angle (error 1.4° for lift, 0.8° for ripper), so the rod stays within 4 cm of the barrel axis even at the extremes.
- The lift cylinders and their lugs hang from a virtual "lift_frame" that does not roll with the tilt. At full tilt the blade slides up to 0.16 m behind the lugs, but the rod never leaves its barrel.
- The ripper barrel joint frame is rotated 180° about the vertical axis so every revolute limit stays within ±0.81 rad, not beyond ±π.
- There are no allowed_overlaps: the push arms stop short of the blade, with a visual-only ball joint between them.

**Cameras** (all on the tractor)
- front: operator eye just outside the windscreen at 2.62 m, pitched 0.42 rad down. It sees the hood, the lift cylinders and the top of the blade, and the blade tilt is clearly visible.
- left/right: on the front corners of the cab roof at 3.15 m, pitched 0.45 rad down and yawed ±0.40 rad outward. They see the blade wings and push arms.

Justified: blade roll about the fore-aft axis is not covered by the raise/out/left (counter-clockwise from above) vocabulary. core_issues: render.py `_draw_ortho`: the 'front' panel draws front-most shapes first (depth = -mean(x), sorted ascending), so the rear of the machine is painted on top. Tail lights and the ripper cover the cab and blade, while +y is still plotted to the right, so the panel is really a mirrored rear view. Using sign +1.0 for the front projection would give a true front view. The 'side' panel is similarly a mirror image: +y shapes on top with +x to the right. I worked around it by checking tilt direction from geometry and my own 3D and camera renders.

checks.py tool-direction vocabulary has no auto-verifiable words for roll/tilt tools (rotation about a fore-aft axis), so 'tilt_left'/'tilt_right' can only produce a warning. Suggestion: add a roll group, e.g. words containing tilt_left/tilt_right checked by the z-change of the +y end of the child subtree.

Followers are limited to k*q_src + c from a single source joint, so parts that depend on two tools (blade lift and blade tilt) cannot be exact. Workaround: a virtual non-rolling 'lift_frame' link carries the lift-cylinder rods and lugs, and the push arms follow the tilt only. A multi-source or point-at follower would remove the up-to-0.16 m blade-to-lug slide at full tilt.

- Extend the ripper-mount box to the new pivot height.

This keeps the -0.60 / +0.55 m tip range but leaves the beam about 0.35 m above grade at full depth. Alternatively, keep the pivots and shorten the depth range, but that departs from the datasheet. Re-check that the cylinder fit stays within 0.03 rad.

issues.description: The right tilt cylinder and left tilt brace are rigid shapes on the push arms and do not extend. Their upper ends move up to about 0.2 m away from the blade lugs at full tilt, so the one actuator that drives the tilt visibly comes off its lug, close to the right camera.
issues.evidence:
FK of the rod/brace upper end (2.66, ±1.30, 1.22 on the push arm) against the blade lug centre (2.65, ±1.29, 1.18):
- at tilt 0: offset (0.005, 0.010, 0.041) m
- at tilt ±0.20, the left brace (tilt -0.2) / right cylinder (tilt +0.2): offset (-0.073, 0.191, 0.064) m
- the same pairs at lift_hi: (-0.086, -0.191, 0.046) m

The lug is only 0.18 m wide (y 1.20-1.38) and the rod is 0.07 m, so the rod end lands outside the lug.
issues.suggested_fix:
Split each cylinder:
- Keep the barrel on the push arm.
- Parent the rod (and the upper half of the brace) to the blade, with its eye on the blade lug, pointing back toward the barrel and long enough to stay inside it across ±0.20 rad.

The rod then stays pinned to the lug and appears to slide in and out of the barrel like a real tilt cylinder. A 1-2 cm axis error is fine for a visual-only part.

issues.description: The sprocket rolling radius does not match the track pitch line, so the cosmetic sprocket spin is about 7% too fast for the track speed.
issues.evidence: The track wraps the sprocket at SPROCKET_WRAP_R = 0.40 m with BELT = 0.09, giving a belt centre-line radius of about 0.355 m. The joints use wheel_radius = SPROCKET_R = 0.33 (lines 510, 513).
issues.suggested_fix: Set wheel_radius = SPROCKET_WRAP_R - BELT / 2 (0.355) and enlarge the visual disc to match, so checks.py's 5% cylinder-radius warning stays quiet. Or reduce SPROCKET_WRAP_R to 0.375.

issues.description: The lift-cylinder rods attach low on the blade back, and their lugs sit on the non-rolling lift_frame, so the blade slides about 0.16 m past them at full tilt.
issues.evidence: LIFT_EYE = (2.56, 0.50) is 0.50 m above the cutting edge, about 35% of the 1.42 m blade height. On D6/D65 the lift-cylinder brackets are on the upper half of the moldboard back. FK: at tilt 0.2, the blade point at (2.6, 0.80, 0.50) drops 0.16 m while the lift_frame lug stays put. The builder acknowledged this.
issues.suggested_fix: Move LIFT_EYE up to about z 0.85-0.95 (the upper box beam is at 1.00-1.30) and re-run the cylinder fit. This also makes the cylinders less steep across the front-camera view. The lug slide needs a multi-source follower (see core issues); otherwise it is acceptable as is.

issues.description: The machine docstring and spec.notes say to verify the tilt in 'the front views of the pose render', but those panels are drawn in reverse depth order (render.py bug), and the report's camera claims rely on the init pose only.
issues.evidence: spec.notes at line 553: 'see the front views of the pose render'. Those panels show the rear (tail lights, ripper shank) painted over the blade. The front-camera claim holds only for the raised blade (1.8% at init vs 0.3% tilted at grade).
issues.suggested_fix: After the render.py fix, refer to the corrected front panel, or say that a pinhole/3D view at grade shows the left (+y) corner low at +0.2. Keep the measured corner heights in the note (left 0.08 m / right 0.74 m at +0.2).

core_issues:
render.py `_draw_ortho` (line 74) uses the wrong depth sign for all three ortho views, not just front and side. With proj = side +1, top -1, front -1 and an ascending sort, the nearest shapes are drawn first and the farthest end up on top. As a result:
- The side panel is a see-through view of the +y side plotted with +x to the right.
- The front panel paints the tail lights and ripper over the blade.
- The 'top' panel is really a bottom view: in bulldozer 'init — top' the dark main frame and tracks cover the cab roof and fenders.
Fix: flip all three signs (side -1.0, top +1.0, front +1.0) or sort in descending order.

checks.py only tests self-overlap and ground clearance in the init pose. Nothing sweeps the tool ranges, so problems at the range extremes (e.g. the bulldozer's ripper carriage and pocket at -0.07 m at full depth) are never flagged. Suggestion: also test each tool's lower/upper limit (and lower/upper combinations) for overlaps, and report, at least as info or warning, the non-tip links that go below grade.

There is no camera-usefulness check. The bulldozer passes every check and test while its front camera shows 0-0.4% blade pixels in working poses. Suggestion: add a check (or a test using a simple ray cast against the collision OBBs) that each tool's child subtree is visible to the front camera at init and at a 'working' pose (e.g. q=0 or the tool's lower limit), and is not just inside the frustum.

checks.py's tool-direction vocabulary has no roll/tilt group, so 'tilt_left'/'tilt_right' can only ever produce a warning. Suggestion: add a roll group that checks the z-change of the +y end of the child subtree. Note that the tilt-direction convention (+1 = left end down) has to be fixed project-wide.

Followers take a single source (q = k*q_src + c), so parts that depend on two tools (lift cylinders against lift + tilt, tilt cylinder length) cannot be exact. This is why the bulldozer has a virtual lift_frame and lugs that slide 0.16 m. A multi-source linear follower (sum of k_i*q_i + c) or a 'point-at' follower for cylinders would remove these workarounds across machines.

The same helpers are copied across machine files: `_rot` (11 files), `_follower` (7), `_cylinder_fit` (5), `_bx` ground-coordinate box (3), `_wrap` (3). Moving them into spec.py (e.g. rot2, follower_joint, fit_cylinder_follower, ground_box) would shorten the machine files and keep the fits consistent.
Not the bulldozer: the full test suite currently fails `test_committed_assets_in_sync` for mini_excavator (its committed URDF is stale). All bulldozer subtests pass.

issues.description: The hook goes below the ground in most scripted episodes. Extending the telescope alone at the travel luff (-0.05 rad) also pushes it in, even with the rope at its minimum. In Isaac the hook block's collision shapes would fight the ground plane while the joint positions are written kinematically, and the hook disappears from the camera images while the instruction says 'lower the hoist to 100%'. The builder compared this to excavator buckets going below grade, but here it is far larger and far more frequent.
issues.evidence: I ran the repo's own tasks.sample_goals from the init pose (4000 seeds) and checked FK at each goal endpoint. In 56.2% of episodes the hook block's collision geometry ends below z=0, and in 66.5% the visual hook does. 86.8% of hoist goals and 45.2% of telescope goals end with the hook in the ground. The worst depth is -13.5 m. At luff -0.05 with rope 0.8 the collision bottom reaches the ground at telescope ~4.9 m (69% of its range), and at full telescope it is -0.34 m (visual -0.76 m). At the init pose any rope above ~1.1 m buries the visual hook. Going the other way, at full telescope and luff >=0.7 the 14 m rope cannot reach the ground at all (the hook stays 7-17 m up). Raising LUFF_LO to 0 cuts bad episodes to 45%. Capping ROPE_MAX at 5-8 m only gets them to ~40%, so constants alone cannot fix this.
issues.suggested_fix: In rough_terrain_crane.py, set LUFF_LO = 0.0 and init = 0.0 (line 77). At 0° the head-pin height does not change with telescope, so the hook stays at about 0.79 m visual / 1.2 m collision above ground in every telescope state. Keep the docstring's -3° datasheet value as a documented deviation. Make the hook-block shapes collision=False so a buried hook cannot jitter the articulation; there is no load physics anyway. The real fix belongs in shared code (see core_issues): an FK-based ground clamp for the hoist in machine_env (rope <= head-pin height - block height), and hoist targets in tasks.sample_goals drawn only from the reachable range.

issues.description: From 57° luff upward, with the rope near its minimum, the hook block passes through the boom head and sections. Self-collision is off, so this is visual clipping, but it happens in a common pose: 'raise the boom luff to 80%' straight from the travel pose. It shows in RViz replays and showcase renders.
issues.evidence: Collision OBB penetration of hook_block vs the boom at rope 0.8 and telescope 0: 0.042 m at luff 1.00, 0.13 m at 1.10, 0.25 m at 1.25-1.35. Visual overlap reaches 0.39 m (boom_base) at 1.35. At 77° the rope must be at least 2.5 m to clear. The cause is that the falls and block hang directly under the head-pin centre (FALL_X ±0.16), and the pin sits only 0.25 m past the fly-section end, 0.12 m below the boom axis.
issues.suggested_fix: Hang the block from ahead of the sheave. Give hoist_joint and every rope_seg_i_joint an origin xyz=(0.40, 0, 0) in the level hook_swivel frame (lines 344-346 and 419-421), or about SHEAVE_R plus a small margin. I checked this in memory: worst hook/boom penetration across luff 1.0-1.35 and telescope 0/7.2 at rope 0.8 goes from 0.25 m to 0.000 m. L becomes 12.59 m, 3% over the envelope, which is fine. Then move the swivel's own falls and the head-sheave visual forward to match.

issues.description: All three cameras look down, so when the boom is luffed up the boom head and hook leave every view. Luff and hoist instructions at working angles therefore have no visual grounding. A real RT cab has a roof window for exactly this reason.
issues.evidence: Front camera (pitch +0.08, half-FOV 46.3°): hook elevation in camera is -12° at init (visible), +33° at 30° luff, +55° at 45° luff, +74° at 60° luff (both out of view), and +51° at 45° luff fully extended (out). Over 600 uniform random tool poses the boom head (hook_swivel) is inside some camera's FOV only 48% of the time. Left and right cameras (pitch 0.30, yaw ±0.65) see it 16-17% of the time. The builder's own cams_both.png shows the left and right views as almost all ground plus a deck corner, and in the working pose the hook sits at the very top edge of the front view.
issues.suggested_fix: Pitch the front camera up, e.g. rpy=(0.0, -0.35, -0.10) on line 489. In my FK test this raises boom-head visibility from 46% to 78% and hook visibility from 71% to 79%, and the travel-pose hook stays in view. Alternatively give the left (cab-roof) camera a negative pitch so it looks up along the boom.

issues.description: In the travel pose the hook is not actually stowed. The visual hook hangs 0.32 m above ground, 3.8 m ahead of the bumper, while the machine drives at up to 11.1 m/s. The 'hook-block tie-down' box on the bumper is decorative and nothing is tied to it.
issues.evidence: FK at init: hook_block frame at x=7.83 m. Lowest visual point 0.315 m and lowest collision point (trunnion) 0.735 m above ground. Site barriers are 0.8 m tall, so the trunnion hits a barrier before the bumper does. The tie-down is at x=4.07-4.12.
issues.suggested_fix: The LUFF_LO=0 change above raises the hook to 0.79 m visual. Otherwise remove the tie-down box, or document that the block hangs free in travel.

issues.description: The lift cylinder is nearly horizontal in travel, and its base sits 0.95 m behind the slew axis, only 0.6 m ahead of the boom foot. On real RT cranes the lift-cylinder base is at or ahead of the slew centre on the turntable front, and the cylinder is visibly inclined. At full luff the barrel also clips into the base section.
issues.evidence: Barrel elevation at init is 4.8° (fit k=0.961, c=0.131). LIFT_BASE=(-0.95, 0.25) and the eye is 4.2 m along the boom, so the stroke is only 1.38 m (3.575 to 4.955 m). Visual OBB overlap lift_cylinder/boom_base is 0.11 m at luff 1.35.
issues.suggested_fix: Move LIFT_BASE forward and down, e.g. to (+0.3..+0.6, 0.15), then re-run _lift_cylinder_fits. Check that the cylinder clears the cab (y>=0.45) and the jib.

issues.description: At full lock the inner steered tyre swings into the carrier frame box. In addition, the knuckle's drawn king pin sits 0.42 m inboard of the actual steer axis (the joint is at the tyre centre), so it orbits through the axle end as the wheel steers.
issues.evidence: At max_steer 0.55 the inner (left) wheel is at 0.645 rad. The tyre's innermost point at frame height reaches |y|=0.354, while the frame box (6.50×0.84) has a half-width of 0.42, so 0.066 m of penetration. The king pin is cyl(0.09, 0.40) at y=-sy*0.42 in the knuckle frame (line 429), but the steer joint is at y=±1.01.
issues.suggested_fix: Narrow the frame box near the front axle (e.g. 0.70 m wide), or reduce the steer joint limit and max_steer slightly. Put the king-pin visual on the steer axis (y=0 in the knuckle), or move the steer joint inboard to the king pin; _steer_y comes from FK, so the Ackermann maths still holds.

issues.description: No hoist rope runs from the winch along the boom to the head sheave. In side and 3/4 views the rope appears only below the head, which is unlike any real crane.
issues.evidence: The superstructure has a winch with rope wraps at x=-2.58. No rope shape exists on boom_base or the sections. The builder's work_raster.png shows a bare boom top.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a thin visual rope on top of each section (boom_base from the winch to its collar, then each section's top to its own collar). Being on the sections, it extends with them.

issues.description: The stowed outrigger pads are the lowest carrier point and sit below the datasheet ground clearance.
issues.evidence: Jack pad box at z=-0.37 (line 261) has its bottom 0.35 m above ground. The axle differentials are at 0.435 m and the docstring gives ground clearance ≈ 0.45 m.
issues.suggested_fix: Raise the stowed jack/pad assembly about 0.10-0.15 m, e.g. pad z=-0.25 and jack cylinder centre -0.10.

issues.description: The file is much heavier than the reference style (constants plus a single build()). It is 504 lines with nine module-level helpers (rod, _rot, _linear_fit, _lift_cylinder_fits, _follower, _tyre, _cab, _section, _stowed_jib) and an assert inside build(). It is readable, but heavy for a spec file.
issues.evidence: hydraulic_excavator.py is 133 lines with no helpers. rough_terrain_crane.py is 504 lines.
issues.suggested_fix: Optional: fold the purely cosmetic helpers (_stowed_jib, the cab trim and the tyre lugs) into shorter shape lists, or move generic ones such as rod/_follower into spec.py if other machines need them too.

core_issues: The 'top' and 'front' panels in render.py (_draw_ortho) are drawn in the wrong order (confirmed by reading the code). proj 'top' = (0,1,2,-1.0) sorts by -z ascending, so the highest shapes are drawn first and the lowest last: a view from below, and on the RTC the carrier hides the superstructure. 'front' = (1,2,0,-1.0) draws the frontmost shapes first: you see the rear while the axes are labelled as a front view. Fix: use sgn=+1.0 for both 'top' and 'front'. The 'side' panel (sgn=+1 on y) is a left-side view mirrored so +x points right, which is consistent.

machine_env and tasks.py have no ground awareness for hoists. For this crane, tasks.sample_goals from the init pose puts the hook below z=0 in 56% of episodes (87% of hoist goals, worst -13.5 m). Proposal: an optional per-joint ground clamp in machine_env, e.g. Joint.min_clearance_link, so each step the rope is limited to the FK head-pin height minus the block height. Also make sample_goals draw hoist targets only from the range reachable in the current pose, or express hoist goals as hook height above ground.

checks.validate only tests self-overlap in the init pose. The RTC's hook block passes 0.25 m (collision) / 0.39 m (visual) through the boom at luff >= 57° with a short rope, and nothing flags it. Suggest also running the overlap test at the default_poses extremes (all tools at lower/upper) and at each tool's endpoints, as warnings.

test_env_logic.test_tools_respect_limits_and_wrap requires every non-continuous tool to cover its full range in 15 s (30*15 steps). That forces 2.5-5× real rates on long-stroke tools (crane luff 0.10 rad/s, telescope 0.5 m/s per section). TaskController already allows 40 s per goal. Suggest running the test for max(15 s, 1.1*(upper-lower)/velocity), or writing the 15 s rule into spec.py and the README.

spec.py has no variable-length visual primitive (a rope or rod between two links). The RTC needs 9 follower rope-segment links (25 links in total) to draw two continuous falls, and still has no rope along the boom.
